💡 Key Takeaways
  • The internet of today is a far cry from the days when Grand Theft Auto 5 was released, which is partly why Rockstar didn't bring back its own satirical version of the web in GTA 6.
  • The web pages of Lifeinvadder, Bleeter, and Eyefind have instead given way to BuckMe, Scooter Bros, and WhatUp apps.
  • Recent findings suggest that "It didn't feel necessary for us," Rockstar North boss Rob Nelson told Kotaku.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The internet of today is a far cry from the days when Grand Theft Auto 5 was released, which is partly why Rockstar didn't bring back its own satirical version of the web in GTA 6.

The web pages of Lifeinvadder, Bleeter, and Eyefind have instead given way to BuckMe, Scooter Bros, and WhatUp apps. The reason? Smartphone apps just made more sense.

Recent findings suggest that "It didn't feel necessary for us," Rockstar North boss Rob Nelson told Kotaku. "We definitely wanted to lean into apps and create these apps.".

According to recent reports, though some of the apps in GTA 6 perform similar tasks to the web of old, Nelson mentioned the team didn't want players to be distracted from the game's detailed open world by staring at screens. That also extends to getting players to appreciate the value of money, and witnessing the progression of Jason and Lucia as they go from pawnshop robberies to staging major bank heists.

"They don't really need websites to be buying a lot of shit, you know what I mean, and so everything grows very organically," Nelson said, adding that websites may return in the future.

Sources indicate that "I remember asking Stu Petri, our head of 2D and UI, about websites, and he was like, 'For what? What do you need it for?' So, that was it," he added.

In materials supplied by Rockstar ahead of our review, Sam Grosset (associate UI director at the studio) also explained that a lot of thought went into how the apps work, and how easily the phone needed to fit into your play style in order for it to work as effectively as possible.

"We ensure the UI feels like a natural extension of the game world, supporting players without interrupting gameplay or breaking immersion, unless necessary to do so," said Grosset. "The UI should be complementary to the game and appropriate for each scenario. It was a big shift for our phone interface to be in-hand, but it supports that feeling of playing as Jason or Lucia and helps us stay embedded in the world.".

Rockstar would continually "raise the bar, question assumptions, explore latest possibilities, and learn through rigorous testing and iteration" in order to make these apps - and the UX/UI in general - feel in line with the production quality of the rest of the game.

In Eurogamer's GTA 6 review, Chris Tapsell awarded the open-world crime game five stars, raving about its absurd level of detail, compelling characters, exciting action and of its major heart.

If you're looking to spend the next several days playing Rockstar's latest hit, Eurogamer's GTA 6 walkthrough has detailed guides on everything from individual missions, to core mechanics like the new Wanted Level, and relationship and romance.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lance Broadway, a former pitcher for the Chicago White Sox and New York Mets, died unexpectedly on Tuesday, November 17. He was 43.

“Some heartbreaking news: Former TCU and DBU pitcher Lance Broadway has passed away,” Jamie Plunkett, a Texas Christian University sports reporter for HornedFrogBlitz.com, declared via X on Wednesday, November 18.

Recent findings suggest that “Broadway earned 2005 CUSA Pitcher of the Year and First-Team All-American honors from Baseball America, posting a 1.61 ERA and 151 strikeouts in 117 innings in his lone season as a Horned Frog,” Plunkett continued. “Following that season, he was selected 15th overall in the 2005 MLB Draft by the Chicago White Sox. He made his MLB Debut on Sept. 7, 2007, and also spent time with the Mets and Blue Jays organizations.”.

The post concluded, “Broadway also briefly stepped into acting, appearing in the 2013 film Olympus Has Fallen as well as a handful of television and short film projects.”.

A cause of death has not yet been revealed.

It has been revealed that broadway was born in Bryan, Texas, in August 1983. He began his college career as a pitcher for Dallas Baptist University while majoring in communications. He earned two all-conference honors at the school before transferring to TCU his junior year.

After college, Broadway spent two years with the White Sox from 2007 to 2009 before he was traded to the Mets in exchange for veteran catcher Ramon Castro.

Check our latest news in Google News.

Check our latest news in Apple News.

It has been revealed that during his time with the Mets, Broadway posted a 6.75 ERA in 14 and two-thirds innings in the 2009 season. He was non-tendered after the season ended and briefly signed with the Toronto Blue Jays in December 2009.

Broadway retired from baseball after the 2010 season and ventured into acting. Along with Olympus Has Fallen, he appeared on the TV demonstrates Saint George, Kevin From Work, Lucifer, Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. and Colony.

It has been revealed that “I originally … in 2010 was my last [MLB] season and in every offseason I wanted to get involved with something,” Broadway told Screen Slam’s Shawn Cauthen in 2013. “And I don’t know why, but I just wanted to go take an improv class. The improv class I wanted didn’t start until January 2011, so I asked a friend who told me to go take an acting class. That way, at least I will be in front of people doing something while they watch. So I got into an acting class in November 2010. I loved it and stuck with it.”.

Virginia Feito on the Film Adaptation of Her Novel ‘Victorian Psycho’

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2097 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The writer is the lowest form of life on a movie.- Martin McDonagh.
  • When I finished editing my second novel, Victorian Psycho, I could not imagine we would be shooting the film adaptation the following year, mere months after the book’s publication.
  • I decided then to undertake this journey that would take me metaphorically to Hollywood but geographically to a county just outside of Dublin, where we would recreate the Ensor House of my novel.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The writer is the lowest form of life on a movie.- Martin McDonagh.

When I finished editing my second novel, Victorian Psycho, I could not imagine we would be shooting the film adaptation the following year, mere months after the book’s publication. Generally, making a movie is one major miracle produced by an amalgamation of thousands of other tiny miracles. But when I met Zach Wigon, I understood that this was a joyfully tenacious person who was going to make this movie if it cost him his life.

I decided then to undertake this journey that would take me metaphorically to Hollywood but geographically to a county just outside of Dublin, where we would recreate the Ensor House of my novel. Among film stars, an Irish crew, and (rumored) ticks, the adaptation of Victorian Psycho—based on my screenplay, which is based on my novel, which is based on my ego, I guess—was born. Throughout the shoot I kept a sort of pseudo diary in order to remember every surreal detail from which I still haven’t recovered. I’ve chosen to reproduce some of it here.

According to recent reports, director Zach Wigon and producer Lisa Kelly call me from the set on the first day of shooting (Zach and I have agreed I won’t visit the set until after the first week so the cast and crew can acclimate without me hovering over them, because I am an intense fame whore, and also, I suppose, to signal I’m not important enough to pull a P.L. Travers and attempt to boycott the movie).

Over the phone, the producer claims she can’t wait to meet in person. I tell her I’m underwhelming.

Industry observers note that they promise to send me the dailies. I spend all day waiting for the dailies. The dailies never come.

Sources indicate that at around 9 p.m., I spiral because I don’t know whether to celebrate with Champagne or KFC. I decide to have both.

Industry observers note that I finally get the dailies. I fall in love with Maika Monroe’s character so hard it’s like I have an obsessive crush circa 2006 whose Facebook photos I’m compulsively looking at. But in this case it’s the same scene throughout five almost identical takes of Maika calling a 10-year-old boy a little idiot.

Over the phone, Zach mentions concerns about a specific scene because we don’t have the budget for that many extras. I get carried away and suggest shipping over a whole battalion of free extras from Spain because, in my head, it’s going to be me and my friends, drunk and decked out in period clothing like we’re at a cheesy bachelorette party. One friend starts making childcare arrangements and another cancels her Holter monitor appointment so she can come to the shoot. What could go wrong?

I start to realize what could go wrong.

I am informed we are probably no longer going to need the extras, and I feel a huge wave of relief as I uninvite my excited friends. I pack a suitcase for Ireland. It weighs 57 pounds.

I have a steak on the plane to Dublin at, like, 3 p.m., because when you’re flying business and somebody offers you steak, you take it.

The hotel room is wonderful, but I jokingly tell Zach over the phone that it’s on a first floor, so someone might crawl up and break in through the window and rape me, and he laughs at first but then is concerned and tells me to request a room on a higher floor, and I tell him it was a joke, but it wasn’t really.

I fill up the hotel room bathtub and call reception for a glass of red wine because I am a queen and I am queening. The glass doesn’t come, so in my anxious impatience I attempt to open a bottle of red wine sitting above the minibar. The cork crumbles because I’ve never understood how to use a corkscrew—like the compass in math class, I just faked my way through it my entire life and hoped for the best. So I call reception for another glass of red wine. They bring me all the glasses of wine and also properly uncork the bottle, and I watch Seinfeld in the bathtub while I drink red wine. I get drunk and paint my nails.

Recent findings suggest that I arrive on set slightly Bromazepamed. It is extremely surreal to exist in a set labeled “Mr. Pounds’s Bedroom.” I am used to living in the fictional world inside my head but not used to it becoming more real than real life itself.

Recent findings suggest that maika hugs me when we meet, and I swallow a sob and refrain from smelling her hair (partly because it is, in fact, a wig). Everyone on set appears so happy to meet me, I suspect a Good Bye, Lenin! situation in which I have been diagnosed with cancer and for some reason the cast and crew all know but I don’t know. This isn’t the plot of Good Bye, Lenin!, but you’ll know what I mean if you’ve seen it.

Zach asks me to read the VOs in every scene, which means I’m in the scene with Ruth Wilson, Jason Isaacs, and Maika, and I’m about to have a stroke.

Jason eats for real in every single take and has already gulped down seven sausage rolls, so if I fuck up my VO, I will kill myself.

Sources indicate that suddenly experiencing fiction collectively feels very superior to experiencing it privately. This does not bode well for the rest of my career as a novelist.

Sources indicate that there is a scene in a cramped drawing room in which I must read the VO, but I’m supposed to hide from the camera, so I crawl on all fours behind an antique couch and grovel my way around the room while the boom op steps on my hands. I secretly think the boom op hates me because I’m always in his way and have an irritating habit of apologizing when he slams into me.

I start developing Irish inflections, so I say it, “I start developing Irish inflections,” but the Irish seem happy about it, so I pursue it.

Recent findings suggest that jason Isaacs starts doing card tricks between takes because Jason Isaacs is actually magic and also indefatigable. Only one thing could ever defeat Jason Isaacs, and it’s the ghost allegedly living on the third floor.

Even though Zach asked me to oversee the second unit, I don’t think anyone believes I’m actually going to do this—and between you and me, I don’t really even know what a second unit is. It doesn’t help I can’t concentrate on what we’re shooting because we’re in the middle of the woods and someone remarked there were ticks, so I’m wrapping Sellotape around my ankles, hoping this way they won’t be able to crawl up my legs.

Like your worst trauma, I insert myself into the movie forever via a small cameo. I literally just have to stand in a wig while I smile and nod, but I do it in such a way that I ruin every single take. “Just smile…like a normal person,” the second-unit director indicates. I reason Zach can just cut me out of the movie, and I will only have wasted everybody’s time and money. There are worse things, like smiling normally but having no cameo. I cope by chewing on another Bromazepam and another chocolate bar. (Every morning I take the chocolate bar from the hotel minibar. It will invariably become an asset in the long afternoons on set, kind of like in prison or high school.).

I change hotel rooms because I have developed an intense FOMO with which I’m always fearing there is a better hotel room for the same price somewhere in the vicinity. This FOMO is also rampant on set between the different units—in the first unit, you have the cinematographer, Nico Aguilar, laughing in the sunlight, talking about color palettes, while in the second unit, we’re shooting clocks and screaming at each other because we still have 17 establishing shots to go.

In a recent development, anyway, I change hotel rooms, and the newly introduced room is so superior to my previous room it’s like an entirely new hotel. I consider changing hotel rooms further. Perhaps I can somehow upgrade my way into a presidential suite.

My parents visit the set. My dad peers over his glasses at the fake lobster cake, and when I tell him the toilets are in trailers, he sighs gravely.

Sources indicate that jason Isaacs convinces my dad to take up tennis again even though my dad’s not supposed to play tennis after his seven hernias. But my dad is so inspired by this actor, who is not a doctor but whose performance in The Patriot my dad can’t help but praise at least once a month, that he will immediately start playing tennis again upon his return to Spain, and whatever medical complications arise henceforth shall all be Jason Isaacs’s fault.

At the Shelbourne restaurant that night, my mom tells the sommelier how she can’t drink red wine anymore because it makes her anxious, and he kneels on the floor beside her and places a hand on his heart as if she were confiding something intimate to him like her fear of death.

Suddenly, real life feels less real than fictional life.

According to recent reports, obama is visiting Dublin and he’s booked the entire floor, so he essentially kicks me out of the Shelbourne (probably to stay in the JFK Suite next door to my room, which is disappointingly predictable), so I go to The Hoxton, because what is life if you’re not constantly changing hotel rooms? The Hoxton is really lovely, but I get OCD about the light bulbs in the room because they appear mismatched, so I ask housekeeping to change them, but they claim not to have any extra light bulbs, which sounds suspect—like, what do they do if a light bulb suddenly goes out? Do they just never replace it?

Recent findings suggest that we end the shoot at 5 a.m. I am wearing a thick puffer coat and a thermal T-shirt and a furry hat, plus fur-lined boots over my Sellotaped ankles, although I wonder, If ticks can survive this temperature, they kind of deserve to live off my blood. Nobody else seems as concerned about the cold as me, but then again, most of them are Irish.

Recent findings suggest that sadly, when we wrap, we are all so exhausted everyone races to clean up and leave, and it is sort of anticlimactic. I don’t know what I was expecting, but balloons falling from the skies did flash through my mind.

In the car on the way to our respective quarters, Zach and I look out the window, wide-eyed, like kidnapped children. Zach starts discussing a new project for us. I wonder if he is a sociopath.

I type this over a year later, sitting at my desk in Madrid, striving to work on my next novel. I feel empty inside knowing there is no car to pick me up and take me to set and thereby escape reality for extended periods of time, until set becomes reality and reality becomes a limbo in which you wait for remarked reality.

I am working on a novel, but also on four new scripts. I hope to return to reality someday.

This story was originally published in Vanity Fair España.

Walmart’s early Black Friday sale just kicked off, offering no shortage of worthy tech deals, and one home audio deal in particular has our attention. If you’re looking to level up your home theater audio setup for less, the Vizio 4.1 Pro SV410YW-10 Soundbar and wireless surround speakers setup with Dolby Atmos and DTS:X support is on sale for $79 (originally $148), a nearly 50% discount.

In a recent development, the two pre-paired wireless surround speakers can be positioned behind or beside your seating area, while two bass drivers built into the 32-inch soundbar mean you don’t need a separate subwoofer. The system maxes out at 95 dB, with bass extending to 50 Hz.

According to recent reports, the SV410YW-1 connects to your television through HDMI eARC and supports CEC, so you can adjust the volume with your TV remote. While its integrated subwoofers won’t give you the same impressive low end as a dedicated unit, this system still delivers robust, bassy sound that goes far beyond built-in TV speakers. There’s an added perk for Vizio TV owners—it can be attached directly beneath the screen using the QuickFit feature.

Along with the deal are additional promos, like up to two free months of Apple Music and up to a free month of Apple TV. If your current TV sound setup is lacking some oomph and you want an under-$100 upgrade with a subwoofer and soundbar, the Vizio 4.1 Pro SV410YW-10 Soundbar and wireless surround speaker combo is a good choice for the money.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Despite its somewhat muted critical reception, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 has predictably topped the US video game charts in October.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Despite its somewhat muted critical reception, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 has predictably topped the US video game charts in October. The Infinity Ward-developed shooter was October's best-selling game in the US across digital and retail, beating the month's other big-hitters, including Gears of War: E-Day and Star Wars: Galactic Racer.

That's according to market analysis firm Circana's latest US market report, which revealed Modern Warfare 4 was October's leader in dollar sales. This marks the 19th-year running that a Call of Duty game topped the charts in its release month, a streak that began with November 2008's COD: World at War.

However, despite a successful October, Modern Warfare 4 hasn't managed to land in Circana's top ten list of year-to-date biggest sellers. In fact, the only COD title on the list is the Black Ops 2 port released this summer. NBA 2K27 continues to lead Circana's ranking, having overtaken Resident Evil: Requiem last month to secure the top spot. It's a reverse of Circana's September report, when NBA 2K27 failed to lead its own debut month but claimed the top spot in the year-to-date list. Here's the list of the top 10 year-to-date:.

Industry observers note that away from Modern Warfare 4, October saw the release of several other well-performing and critically acclaimed games, and six of the top ten were new releases. That hasn't stopped Circana from posting 14 percent lower spending on games compared to October last year. Analyst Mat Piscatella noted much of that dip can be attributed to a massive slump in mobile spending, and also because October 2025 was particularly strong, with both Battlefield 6 and Pokémon Legends: Z-A releasing. Here's October's top 10:.

In Eurogamer's Modern Warfare 4 review, Dom Peppiatt awarded it four stars, writing: "Modern Warfare 4 represents the highest tide for Call of Duty in seven years. Infinity Ward needed to pull off a balancing act I don't envy; injecting just enough nostalgia into a series propped up with so many conventions and expectations there's barely room for anything fresh, alongside enough innovation and intrigue to keep people interested.".

If you haven’t heard already: Grand Theft Auto 6, finally out now on PS5 and Xbox, is a very big video game. It’s also one of the best games I’ve played in years. And one reason I love it so much is because of all the great music on the in-game radio stations. There are so many songs. In fact, just two of the game’s biggest radio stations contain more songs than all of GTA: Vice City’s radio stations combined did back on the PS2.

Recent findings suggest that two of the biggest radio stations inÂ GTA 6Â are FLASH FM, a pop station, and V-ROCK, a classic rock station. Funnily enough, both of these stations appeared in Vice City, too. But this time around, the stations have a lot more music. Let’s do some number crunching!

Recent findings suggest that in GTA: Vice City‘s version of V-Rock, there were (before some songs were cut in later ports for licensing reasons) 17 songs. Meanwhile, Vice City‘s Flash FM featured 15 songs. And in total, there were 106 songs in GTA 6 across its various stations. In GTA 6, Flash FM alone now boasts 80 songs, according to Rockstar’s recently released credits. And V-Rock now has 70 songs. Combined, there are more songs on just these two stations than in all of Vice City.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For those still waiting for GTA 6 to unlock, it's possible you have something of a mistaken impression of what the early hours will look like. Despite partially sharing a setting with GTA Vice City, you should not expect to be walking up the game's equivalent of Ocean Drive and Miami Beach in the opening minutes, as in the 2002 game. Far from it. As we noted in our video discussion on why we gave GTA 6 a 10/10 in our review, Tamoor and Jake did some expectation-setting. Rather than starting the game in Vice City, you'll instead spend the opening hours in a smaller corner of the state of Leonida, Key Lento. Vice City is undoubtedly the crown jewel of the game's world, but it could be as much as 20 hours before you reach it, depending on how you play. This seems to be a deliberate decision that, as Tam says, allows you to progress through the world at roughly the same pace as the ambitions of co-stars Lucia and Jason. The opening area may not be as glamorous as Vice City, but it is no less detailed than the rest of the game. It's possible it's only meant to last you around 5-6 hours, but we found it easy to get lost spending far more time than that, which resulted in Tam not reaching Vice City until after 15 or 16 hours. https://www.youtube.com/shorts/XkHgrxN3R4g Key Lento provides a good look at how the game and its simulation work, letting you eventually progress to a much larger space (seriously, the map is huge) with a good understanding of how things work. All of this is to say, the glitz and glamor of Vice City are waiting for you--eventually. To make the most of the opening hours, be sure to check out our guide on what to do in GTA 6 first.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Pour one out for the PC gamers who are now forced to watch everyone frolic in the streets of Grand Theft Auto 6 on consoles this week.
  • Industry observers note that you might assume GTA 5 player counts would tank now that it's old news, but the numbers have actually jumped up a bit in the last month.
  • In fact, GTA 5 has steadily kept a good amount of players over the last year, with major spikes happening around the occasional price discount.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pour one out for the PC gamers who are now forced to watch everyone frolic in the streets of Grand Theft Auto 6 on consoles this week. The next best thing on PC is GTA 5, and its recent Steam concurrents suggest people are trying their best to fight the FOMO until Rockstar decides to bring the new one over.

Industry observers note that you might assume GTA 5 player counts would tank now that it's old news, but the numbers have actually jumped up a bit in the last month. SteamDB indicates a peak of around 87,000 concurrent players in the last day, an almost 10% increase from October. There's been a bit of a dip today—which could partially be attributed to GTA 6 finally becoming available in every region—but it's not as sharp of a drop as you'd think it'd be for a 13-year-old game.

In fact, GTA 5 has steadily kept a good amount of players over the last year, with major spikes happening around the occasional price discount. It usually hovers around 40,000 to 50,000 average concurrent players, and GTA 6's release hasn't broken the pattern. That's the beauty of PC gaming for you: Steam sales and mods keep games like this chugging along years after they'd be considered cutting edge.

GTA 5 holdouts might have a long road ahead of them though. GamesBeat reported last month that "four industry sources familiar with the studio's prepares" noted GTA 6 will make its way to PC in the first three months of 2027. In the past, Rockstar held PC releases back for at least seven months (GTA 5 PC took a year and six months), so an early 2027 release would be unorthodox if the report is true.

According to recent reports, GTA Online, or some kind of multiplayer mode, will hopefully come at some point and it would make some sense to drop it at the same time as a PC release, or at least that's what I tell myself at night. I've only played a few hours of the game and I'm already imagining the kinds of mods that will inevitably show up in the first week. Someone is going to make it so Jason can instantly gulp down his coffee for the stamina buff, I know it.

For now, PC players will just have to continue biding their time in GTA 5 and pray that Rockstar at the very least announces a GTA 6 PC release date sooner rather than later.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Closing statements in Rockstar and IWGB's employment tribunal case - revolving around the GTA 6 developer's alleged 'union busting' and the firing of 34 employees - have now been read, bringing the hearing to an end.
  • The case, which began in September and has included evidence from 23 claimants in the months since, must now be considered by the judge, who will determine if Rockstar unfairly dismissed employees in breach of their employment rights.
  • Sources indicate that people Makes Games' Chris Bratt has been following the case closely and reporting on proceedings as they've unfolded.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Closing statements in Rockstar and IWGB's employment tribunal case - revolving around the GTA 6 developer's alleged 'union busting' and the firing of 34 employees - have now been read, bringing the hearing to an end. There's at the moment no timeline for a verdict, however, with one commentator suggesting a judgement could take weeks or months to arrive.

The case, which began in September and has included evidence from 23 claimants in the months since, must now be considered by the judge, who will determine if Rockstar unfairly dismissed employees in breach of their employment rights. Rockstar has been accused of unlawfully firing workers for being part of a union, but the GTA developer insists employees were dismissed for breaching confidentiality agreements.

Sources indicate that people Makes Games' Chris Bratt has been following the case closely and reporting on proceedings as they've unfolded. With closing statements now complete, Bratt quoted Judge Lucy Wiseman as saying, "I cannot give a time frame for producing the judgement in this case. What I will say is that I will use my best endeavors to get that judgement out as rapidly as I possibly can.".

However, Bratt suggests it could be ""anywhere from a few weeks up to a few months before we actually hear the judgement", noting "The firings themselves, let's not forget, happened over a year ago now. This has been a slog.".

One fired Rockstar worker involved in the case spoke with Bratt after the closing statements to share their thoughts. "Honestly it's just sort of blended together," they noted. "It’s been so long, that after the first six months or so it became the new depressing reality. I'm hoping the judgement will release us from it.".

Last month, the conclusion of the tribunal hearing was delayed after cross examination of witnesses ran long.

Sources indicate that yesterday's closing statements come at a time when all eyes are on GTA 6 as it finally releases this week, concluding years of development for both current and former employees. Many of those workers involved in the case urged players to support the game despite the legal dispute.

In a recent development, additionally, Rockstar employees are currently voting on whether they want recognised union representation at the studio. If the vote passes, it would be the largest recognised union across the entirety of the UK video game industry. The deadline for union votes is 26th November.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As GTA 6 finally arrives, increasingly outspoken games industry legend Warren Spector - known for seminal immersive sims including Deus Ex - has offered both praise for the game's achievements and lambasted its "billion dollar" development model, writing, "I just hope GTA 6 is the last of its kind even if it’s the best we have to offer".

Sources indicate that spector announced his retirement from games development in August following struggles at his OtherSide Entertainment studio, and has been vocal about the state of the games industry in the months since, notably saying anyone at EA responsible for the "travesty" of BioWare's closure should be "ashamed". And now Spector has taken on GTA 6.

In a recent development, "First, congratulations to everyone who worked on GTA 6. It looks like it will be a high point of sorts for our medium and our business," he wrote in a post on LinkedIn. "However… its billion dollar development cost and an undoubtedly crazy marketing budget don't represent a business model anyone else can or probably should emulate.

"That's especially true," Spector continued, "when thousands of developers are out of work. A billion dollars pays for a lot of games and a lot of salaries. Personally I'd rather have hundreds of games and full employment than one game no matter how amazing it is.".

The "sure success" of GTA 6 proves a point he's made "for years", he noted: "That no game that matters ships on time and/or on budget". Highlighting GTA 6's year-long delay and reported billion dollar budget, Spector suggested, "Give a game the time and money to prove its potential (key word, potential) and you have a chance of making something great. Underfund a game or force it out the door before it's ready [is] guaranteed failure no matter how much potential it has.

"So, again, congratulations," Spector concluded. "Ambition and innovation are necessary for the medium to reach its potential. I just hope GTA 6 is the last of its kind even if it's the best we have to offer.".

Despite Spector's concerns, GTA 6's arrival is, as expected, already causing shockwaves across the industry. It has broken pre-order records for Xbox and PlayStation stores, smashed the all-time livestream viewer record, and apparently briefly broke Reddit too. And is its success deserved? Eurogamer's Chris Tapsell thinks so, saying it "pushes back the horizon of video games once again" in his five star GTA 6 review.

He was on paid administrative leave, his school email was frozen, and he assumed this was about him and me. He called what he had done to me a relationship. He didn’t regret his feelings for me. Could I call him when his wife was out of the house?

I was thirty-seven years old. I was a few weeks out from my partnership interview at a New York law firm. I had a husband and a three-year-old son. I spend my working life telling clients which sentences will look bad in discovery. I read that text twice, and my first thought was, How can I help him?

In a recent development, he had spent years teaching me to use his word for it. It was never a relationship. He groomed me, he exploited me, and he raped me.

It has been revealed that vanity Fair has written about that morning before. Evgenia Peretz opened “Girls, Interrupted” with that text in January 2025, and she went back to Miss Hall’s last fall after the investigation came out. In March, Dan Adler covered the indictment. This time I’m telling it myself.

Later that morning an email arrived from an attorney in Boston. Subject line: “Reaching out about Miss Hall’s School.” I didn’t open it right away. I didn’t need to. Some part of me had been composing that email in my head since I was a teenager. The attorney represented a woman named Melissa Fares, a Miss Hall’s alumna who had been there a few years after me. I had never heard her name.

She had heard mine. Years earlier, older girls at the school had told her about me. She held on to my name, and when she went to a lawyer she remembered it. By then I had married and changed it, and they found me anyway.

I called Matt and asked. “Who is Melissa?” There was a pause long enough to hear him decide something, then a sigh, and then he told me he had had sex with Melissa while she was a student.

Industry observers note that here is what I did next, and I’d ask you to withhold judgment. I told him I would call the lawyer, find out what she had, and report back.

It has been revealed that that’s what twenty-two years of being groomed looks like at a desk in Midtown. You don’t make a decision. The decision was made for you a long time ago, in a dorm room, and you’re simply carrying it out.

Industry observers note that I did call the lawyer. And when I heard my own voice say “I’m not ready to talk to you, I want to talk to Melissa,” I think that was the first sentence in two decades that I stated entirely for myself.

Melissa called that afternoon. I don’t remember how she started. I remember what I said before she got far.

“I’ve been waiting for your call for twenty years.”.

Sources indicate that I meant it literally. Some part of me had always known I wasn’t the only one. I just couldn’t go looking. I could only wait to be found.

Hilary Simon and Melissa Fares, photographed in Far Rockaway, New York, 2025.

Recent findings suggest that she told me her story, and I heard my own memories come out of a stranger’s mouth. He called her “Little One.” He called me “Little One.” He took her to the same hotel in Northampton. He told her he would kill himself if she ever told anyone, which is a thing he had also told me, more than once, in nearly the same words. He had made himself the center of her emotional world before he ever touched her. He had a script.

Sources indicate that for twenty years he had me believing that what happened was singular, and that it was my fault. By the end of that call it was a pattern, and I was a data point. I was not special. It is a strange thing to grieve, not being special to the person who hurt you. I grieved it anyway.

After more than three decades teaching at that school, he resigned the same day.

I arrived at Miss Hall’s, an all-girls boarding school in Pittsfield, Massachusetts, in the fall of 2001. I was fourteen, homesick, and like every other girl my age, positive I was more grown up than I was.

Industry observers note that rutledge had been teaching history there for a decade. He was a massive man with a booming voice, married with two daughters. He lived with his family in a school-owned house across the street from the main entrance. He used to cut the lunch line announcing himself as “Mr. Wonderful.” Girls talked about him like he was a minor deity. They also mentioned, in the breezy way teenagers mention terrible things, that he had a type.

Some evenings, he was one of the adults who did bed checks in the dorms. The others always stood in the doorway. He came in and sat on the edge of my bed.

Sources indicate that by the next fall he was my advisor and my cross-country coach. There was no door at that school he couldn’t open. On the long drives to meets, he told me to sit next to him in the school van. He called me his copilot. The rest of the team sat behind us. He would put his hand on my upper thigh, or pull me close until our legs were touching. I watched the Berkshire hills go by and tried not to look down.

That was the first line he crossed. I was fifteen. After that he crossed them one at a time until there were none left. He kept abusing me for years after I graduated.

From the outside, those years looked like a success story.

I went to college and then law school. I became a civil defense attorney. I got married. I had a son. I was good at my job.

I could find the unanswered email in ten thousand pages of discovery. The report nobody followed up on. I couldn’t open my own file.

Sources indicate that when I tell this story, people ask me some version of the same question. How did nobody notice?

In the late 1990s, years before I ever set foot on Miss Hall’s campus, a student stood up at a school meeting and noted Mr. Rutledge was having sex with another student. The school suspended her for the rest of the year, barred her from graduation and made her write him an apology letter. He kept teaching.

Industry observers note that on my graduation day, Rutledge kissed me and told me that he loved me. A classmate told a staff member, who reported it to the administration. In a memo, Rutledge admitted telling me he loved me but said “[it was] not a romantic expression.” He denied the kiss. They took his word for it. No one called me or my parents.

Hilary Simon on graduation day.

In a recent development, A few years later, after a family reported that he had made advances toward their daughter, the head of school at that time, Jeannie Norris, put a warning to Rutledge in writing. “This isn’t the 70s or the 80s,” she wrote. “Society has no stomach for any kind of inappropriate behavior between adults and girls or teachers and students.” She was worried about the school’s reputation, and about his. In the letter she stated the incident had “the potential for seriously damaging the School and your [Rutledge’s] reputation.” He was not fired.

Over the years that followed Rutledge was made chair of the history department and collected faculty honors. More than one person gave the school my name as a girl he had singled out. Nobody ever called me. In June 2023, I heard another alumna tried to raise concerns about him with the head of school at that time. He was still teaching nine months later, when Melissa reported him.

Recent findings suggest that in August 2025 Miss Hall’s published the results of an outside investigation it had commissioned from Aleta Law. The investigators substantiated grooming and abuse by Rutledge involving at least five students. They found school leadership had been warned about him over the years and hadn’t acted. Staff members told investigators they had suspected him and kept quiet, some because they feared retaliation, others because they assumed no one in charge would listen.

It went beyond Rutledge. The investigation found that seven other Miss Hall’s employees had engaged in sexual misconduct with students, dating back to the 1940s. Eight adults across eighty plus years. That’s a culture of abuse.

It has been revealed that A Berkshire County grand jury has since indicted Norris on a charge of reckless endangerment of a child. She has pleaded not guilty. Another former Miss Hall’s teacher has been indicted for assault with intent to rape and indecent assault and two counts battery of a student. He has also pleaded not guilty.

Recent findings suggest that I read all sixty pages of the Aleta Law report in one sitting. Nothing in it surprised me. It still knocked the air out of me to see my adolescence reduced to numbered findings.

Melissa arrived at Miss Hall’s in 2007, two years after I left.

People sometimes call us friends. That’s true, but it’s a small word for it. I call her my sister survivor.

Industry observers note that I wouldn’t be writing this if Melissa hadn’t gone first. She went to the school alone. In April 2024, she told her story publicly. A few weeks later, I told mine. Then other women came forward. They remarked Rutledge had abused them too.

In October 2024, the Berkshire district attorney mentioned he didn’t believe he could charge Rutledge. In Massachusetts, the age of consent is sixteen. Under the law, a teacher could claim that a sixteen- or seventeen-year-old student had consented.

According to recent reports, melissa and I set out to change the law. We testified at the State House and knocked on every door that would open. Enough Abuse, a Massachusetts nonprofit, had been fighting for this for years. Two national advocacy groups, World Without Exploitation and I Have The Right To, stood with us. Representatives Leigh Davis and John Lawn pushed for it in the House, and Senator Joan Lovely added it to the state budget. In July, Governor Healey signed the Trusted Adults Act.

In Massachusetts, it is now a felony for a teacher or coach to have sex with a student under eighteen.

Melissa and I spoke at the signing ceremony. I stood right next to the governor and thought about the girl in the front seat of the school van, with her teacher’s hand on her leg.

It has been revealed that while we were working on the law, Massachusetts State Police and a latest team of prosecutors in the Berkshire district attorney’s office had reopened the investigation into Rutledge. Melissa and I testified before a grand jury. In March, he was indicted on three counts of rape.

In April, he was arraigned. It was the first time Melissa and I faced him together. In the courtroom, I handed out orange heart stickers. Orange is Melissa’s favorite color. When we saw Rutledge, we both went numb. We had learned to do that as girls, when going somewhere else in our heads was the only way through. He pleaded not guilty.

In a recent development, I looked back at the benches. They were full of orange. Teachers from Miss Hall’s, people from the community, alumnae across generations. I had been alone with this since I was fifteen. That day, a whole room sat behind us. Afterward, Melissa told reporters that for the first time, she held the power in a room with him. I felt it too.

Recent findings suggest that this month, nine years after #MeToo took off, a jury in London convicted Russell Brand of one rape and three sexual assaults. A judge sentenced him to ten and a half years in prison. His crimes went back to 2004. Brand’s attorneys argued the women had waited too long to be believed. I waited twenty years. Delay is often the most ordinary fact in these cases.

Industry observers note that in the midterms, Ohio elected Amy Acton governor. A few weeks before the vote, her opponent’s campaign ran an ad in which her estranged mother called her a liar. Acton’s stepfather had been charged with raping her when she was a child. Republicans and Democrats both condemned the ad. She won anyway.

I watched the returns on election night and thought about the girls at Miss Hall’s who told the truth and were called liars. Survivors get called liars all the time. We almost never get to watch one win.

Tarana Burke knew survivors weren’t being believed long before most people were listening. She started saying “me too” in 2006 to reach Black girls who had survived sexual violence, more than ten years before it became a hashtag. Every survivor who spoke after her made it a little easier for the next one.

In November 2024, a Cornell student told campus police and the Title IX office that she had been gang-raped at a fraternity house weeks earlier. No one has been charged. Cornell’s president set up a task force on sexual assault, but he later admitted he never checked how her case ended.

When I read that, I was back at Miss Hall’s on graduation day, waiting for a phone call that nobody made.

In a recent development, the Epstein survivors know that silence too. For decades, powerful people looked away. Last year survivors pushed Congress to pass a law requiring the Justice Department to release its Epstein files. Millions of pages came out. There have been no arrests in the United States.

Recent findings suggest that I’m still hopeful. Survivors everywhere keep coming forward, and some of the people in charge are finally acting. My body knew what Rutledge had done to me long before I let myself say it aloud. I didn’t have the words. Survivors today do, and they have each other. Melissa found me.

The criminal case against Rutledge isn’t over. His lawyer has asked a judge to dismiss all charges. We don’t know yet whether there will be a trial. Whatever the judge decides, I’ve already reached my own verdict. I’m healing and Rutledge doesn’t get a say in that.

For most of my life, I carried shame that was never mine. He handed it to me. Every adult who looked away handed me a little more.

Predators don’t work alone. Someone always sees something. In the movie Spotlight, a lawyer indicates that if it takes a village to raise a child, it takes a village to abuse one. My village saw. The people in charge did nothing.

Industry observers note that I’ve given the shame back. It belongs to him, and to the people who could have stopped him.

If you are a survivor and you are still carrying shame, you can put it down.

Recent findings suggest that borrow my courage if you need it. Melissa lent me hers.

Industry observers note that neither Matthew Rutledge nor Jean Norris responded to Vanity Fair for the original story, and neither of them has made direct statements to the press. Norris, through her attorney, claimed not to know that Rutledge abused students.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Two men were found dead inside of a home in Gillespie County, Texas, after a hostage situation resulted in an apparent murder-suicide, according to authorities.

The Gillespie County Sheriff’s Office remarked in a press release shared via Facebook that deputies responded to a home on Cemetery Road in Stonewall, Texas, shortly after 5 p.m. on Wednesday, November 18, after they received reports of a disturbance that involved a man with a gun.

Deputies began communicating with the victim inside the residence via phone during the incident, and he told deputies that an armed man would not allow him to leave the home.

Because the incident was treated as a hostage situation, deputies made multiple attempts to communicate with both the suspect and victim so that the conflict could hopefully end in a peaceful resolution.

Authorities stated they lost communication with the men for several hours. Law enforcement then entered the home around 3:30 a.m. on Thursday, November 19, and they found both men dead in a room.

Investigators ultimately determined that the incident was a murder-suicide involving a 35-year-old suspect and a 49-year-old victim.

The Gillespie County Sheriff’s Office mentioned that they worked on the case with the help of the Kerr County Sheriff’s Office Special Operations Unit, Texas Department of Public Safety Special Operations Unit and a Texas Ranger.

It has been revealed that authorities have not yet released the men’s identities as they await to notify next of kin. It’s not right now clear how the two men knew each other or if authorities believe there was a motive in the case.

“More information will be released as the investigation is completed. We will not release any names pending notification of next of kin,” the sheriff’s office concluded in the press release. “Please keep the families in your thoughts and prayers during this very difficult time.”.

And for all the families affected, and the neighbors will have to continue to remember,” one person commented, and another chimed in, “Such a tragedy. Thankful for all the law enforcement personnel and their attempts at a more positive outcome.”.

Industry observers note that microsoft and Take-Two recently announced a deal to allow people to stream Rockstar's GTA 6, and that significantly increases the game's addressable market on Xbox and means people can play the game for as little as $92. This is according to a newly issued report from Ampere Analysis, which said the streaming deal could reach the estimated 10 million "active" Xbox One consoles out there and expand the total addressable market for GTA 6 on Xbox by 30%. For anyone just catching up, Microsoft worked out a deal with Take-Two to allow GTA 6 to be streamed to an Xbox console--that could be an Xbox Series X, Xbox Series S, or even an Xbox One. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rAhUXOYNuH4 There are some key things to know, including how the game streams from an Xbox Series S version of the game and your streaming experience will depend on the strength and consistency of your connection. A report from Digital Foundry said the Xbox Series S edition of GTA 6 struggles with its frame rate at some points, but that might not be an concern for everyone. No such arrangement is in place for PlayStation, so the only way to stream GTA 6, at least right now, is on Xbox. Ampere said there are about 25 million PS4 consoles in the market that are still active, while Sony is the market leader for current-generation consoles with the PS5. Why do a deal with Microsoft and not Sony? Ampere said Take-Two was likely interested in the potential expanded reach with Xbox to help sell more units, but there might have also been a "direct payment" or a revenue-share agreement on Xbox that was more preferential to Take-Two. Ampere said Take-Two wants the PS4 audience as well via streaming, but that might not happen until 2027 at the soonest, if such a deal ever materializes at all. Beyond this, Ampere said there could be "technology-based reasons" why Sony didn't get a deal done for GTA 6 streaming. The research firm pointed out how Microsoft is a "hyperscaler" when it comes to streaming via its vast Azure network, which "puts it in a stronger position to serve a large influx of consumers streaming a brand-newly introduced game like GTA 6 compared to Sony."  Lucia in GTA 6. "The favorable distribution costs to Microsoft as the service provider and owner of the cloud infrastructure also gives it a commercial advantage," Ampere said. "While PS5 users can generally stream their owned games as long as they have an active PS Plus Premium subscription, PS4 users don’t have that functionality. Essentially, Sony is not set up to offer its PS4 users the same streaming experience." Beyond all this, Ampere highlighted how PS5 users ($731) are spending more than PS4 users ($580) over the same lifecycle stage of each console. "Converting users to PS5 is more key to Sony than adding some sales of GTA 6 or PS4 users," Ampere said. Under $100 to play GTA 6 on Xbox Xbox's streaming deal for GTA 6 also makes Xbox the most affordable place to play GTA 6. Ampere said the total cost to play on Xbox could be $92, assuming the player already has an Xbox One, a copy of GTA 6, a controller, and a screen. Ampere did the math by estimating the cost to be 0.24 cents per hour to stream the game, for a total of $92 via streaming, assuming a 50-hour runtime for the game. This rate leaves little margin for Xbox, Ampere said, but the fact that people have to buy streaming time up front means there will no doubt be "a significant amount of playtime languishing in accounts that is never used." As announced previously, people can stream GTA 6 to their Xbox console via a Game Pass membership or by purchasing time without a Game Pass membership. The pricing is below. Cloud playtime packs pricing: 10 hours for $4 25 hours for $8 50 hours for $12 Coinciding with GTA 6's release and the new streaming deal, Microsoft just instituted limits on how many hours members can stream before being asked to pay more. These are: Game Pass Ultimate: 15 hours Game Pass Premium: 10 hours Game Pass Essential: 5 hours Even beyond the streaming deal, Xbox is the most affordable place to play GTA 6 considering that a new Xbox Series S console costs $500, compared to $600 for the cheapest new PS5. Microsoft and Take-Two recently announced a deal to allow people to stream Rockstar's GTA 6, and that significantly increases the game's addressable market on Xbox and means people can play the game for as little as $92.

This is according to a newly issued report from Ampere Analysis, which stated the streaming deal could reach the estimated 10 million "active" Xbox One consoles out there and expand the total addressable market for GTA 6 on Xbox by 30%.

For anyone just catching up, Microsoft worked out a deal with Take-Two to allow GTA 6 to be streamed to an Xbox console--that could be an Xbox Series X, Xbox Series S, or even an Xbox One.

Industry observers note that there are some key things to know, including how the game streams from an Xbox Series S version of the game and your streaming experience will depend on the strength and consistency of your connection. A report from Digital Foundry mentioned the Xbox Series S edition of GTA 6 struggles with its frame rate at some points, but that might not be an issue for everyone.

It has been revealed that no such arrangement is in place for PlayStation, so the only way to stream GTA 6, at least right now, is on Xbox. Ampere said there are about 25 million PS4 consoles in the market that are still active, while Sony is the market leader for current-generation consoles with the PS5.

Recent findings suggest that why do a deal with Microsoft and not Sony? Ampere said Take-Two was likely interested in the potential expanded reach with Xbox to help sell more units, but there might have also been a "direct payment" or a revenue-share agreement on Xbox that was more preferential to Take-Two. Ampere said Take-Two wants the PS4 audience as well via streaming, but that might not happen until 2027 at the soonest, if such a deal ever materializes at all.

In a recent development, beyond this, Ampere said there could be "technology-based reasons" why Sony didn't get a deal done for GTA 6 streaming. The research firm pointed out how Microsoft is a "hyperscaler" when it comes to streaming via its vast Azure network, which "puts it in a stronger position to serve a large influx of people streaming a brand-newly introduced game like GTA 6 compared to Sony.".

"The favorable distribution costs to Microsoft as the service provider and owner of the cloud infrastructure also gives it a commercial advantage," Ampere said. "While PS5 people can generally stream their owned games as long as they have an active PS Plus Premium subscription, PS4 users don’t have that functionality. Essentially, Sony is not set up to offer its PS4 users the same streaming experience.".

Beyond all this, Ampere highlighted how PS5 users ($731) are spending more than PS4 users ($580) over the same lifecycle stage of each console. "Converting users to PS5 is more key to Sony than adding some sales of GTA 6 or PS4 users," Ampere said.

Xbox's streaming deal for GTA 6 also makes Xbox the most affordable place to play GTA 6. Ampere said the total cost to play on Xbox could be $92, assuming the player already has an Xbox One, a copy of GTA 6, a controller, and a screen.

Ampere did the math by estimating the cost to be 0.24 cents per hour to stream the game, for a total of $92 via streaming, assuming a 50-hour runtime for the game.

This rate leaves little margin for Xbox, Ampere remarked, but the fact that people have to buy streaming time up front means there will no doubt be "a significant amount of playtime languishing in accounts that is never used.".

According to recent reports, as confirmed previously, people can stream GTA 6 to their Xbox console via a Game Pass membership or by purchasing time without a Game Pass membership. The pricing is below.

Coinciding with GTA 6's release and the new streaming deal, Microsoft just instituted limits on how many hours members can stream before being asked to pay more. These are:.

Even beyond the streaming deal, Xbox is the most affordable place to play GTA 6 considering that a latest Xbox Series S console costs $500, compared to $600 for the cheapest new PS5.

GTA 6 officially launches for everyone on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Meanwhile, you can check out our GTA 6 guides hub for more details on how to make the most out of your trip to Vice City.

Latest Update: Does GTA 6 have an 'easy mode'? Not officially, but there are two very vital settings you can change to make the game less difficult

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By now, you've probably heard that you cannot use cheats in GTA 6 until you complete the main story.
  • But, for anyone looking to have a slightly easier time with GTA 6 than the dev's intended experience, I come with good news: you can make the game a little bit easier by toggling two options in the game's Settings menu.
  • It has been revealed that 'Accessible Combat' decreases enemy health and makes them deal less damage to your character — the kind of rebalancing that you'd expect from a traditional difficulty slider.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By now, you've probably heard that you cannot use cheats in GTA 6 until you complete the main story. Not only that, but enabling cheat codes also locks story progression and deactivates the ability to save. Basically, you can use cheats to have a quick crime spree and blow off some steam, then it's back to normalcy. Understandably, some gamers are a little put out with this change.

But, for anyone looking to have a slightly easier time with GTA 6 than the dev's intended experience, I come with good news: you can make the game a little bit easier by toggling two options in the game's Settings menu. If you open Settings, and then navigate to Gameplay, you'll find 'Accessible Combat' and 'Reduced Vehicle Damage' toggles. You can activate both to make GTA 6's more difficult elements a little bit easier to work through.

It has been revealed that 'Accessible Combat' decreases enemy health and makes them deal less damage to your character — the kind of rebalancing that you'd expect from a traditional difficulty slider. 'Reduced Vehicle Damage', as you'd expect, lowers the damage taken by your vehicle and allows your ride to endure more punishment. This applies to gunfire, environmental threats, and impact damage.

Toggle these settings comes with a warning from Rockstar, though. A prompt notes that enabling these modifiers will "significantly change the balance and experience of the gameplay". I've been playing around with these settings and whilst they are not a foolproof 'God Mode' by any means, you can absolutely see a difference in the game when they're enabled: Jason and Lucia take a lot more punishment from melee damage and gunshots, and I had to really try to get Jason's old banged up pickup into even the 'slightly smoking' bracket of disrepair. Your mileage may vary, but these settings, from what I can tell so far, certainly do make the game easier.

Given that cheats disable trophies and progression, these settings might be something to keep in mind if you're trying to find a smoother path through the main story of GTA 6. It's a credit to Rockstar's accessibility teams that these have been included at all - alongside the 23 other gameplay accessibility options, the 12 display options, the 70 UI options, the 24 camera options, and the 14 audio options.

Recent findings suggest that "We create inclusive, intuitive, and immersive experiences for every player," noted Rockstar's associate UI director, Sam Grosset, in materials provided to Eurogamer ahead of the game's launch. "Accessibility is considered from the outset, and designing for diverse needs enables us to create better games for everyone. We wanted every player in GTA 6 to have options to play the game how they like. Whether it's selecting a larger font size, opting for a more minimal screen experience, or making a controls tweak to sprinting... the choices are open to all.".

We also learned yesterday that Rockstar has made GTA 6 missions "harder to fail" by making them more open-ended, and giving players more ways to figure out how to do things in their own way.

If you need a hand with any of the myriad things GTA 6 asks you to do, you can read Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Queen's Domain has, by my count, four categories of collectible you have to hoover up if you want to see its more hidden endings, and some of them are real bastards to find⁠—I'd resigned myself to queueing up guides on YouTube to get it all done.

Recent findings suggest that guides are great, you might still need them for some of the collectibles, and if there's one game that feels like it was designed with Google/Reddit/forum help in mind, it's Queen's Domain. But I was thrilled to discover that, very late in the game, Queen's Domain provides a waypoint tool to guide you to its hidden collectibles. It turned what I worried would be a tedious process into yet another example of this game's boundless capacity for surprise and discovery.

I know I would have appreciated the heads-up, the permission to not worry about finding them all earlier in my playtime. If that's how you felt, and you aren't looking for spoilers, great: You can stop reading here. Granted, the spoilers in Queen's Domain are so absurd and out there as to be incomprehensible to someone early on in a playthrough.

There are two requirements to get homing compass guidance in Queen's Domain: You need a fully kitted-out Mask of Second Sight, and to discover the hidden Petrified Garden zone. You can technically reach the latter from very early in the game, but you won't be able to open the necessary path until you acquire all of the lenses for the mask. Here's a quick checklist:.

That's basically, like, the entire third act of the game and encompasses most of the requirements for Queen's Domain's second of four endings⁠—this is super lategame stuff.

You can reach the Petrified Garden by jumping off the teleporter platform while you're in the spacey void warping between zones. The large platform to the side you can dash to is a boss arena⁠—kill the familiar-looking guy here to reawaken the very high-level enemies in the garden.

From there, you can find four god seals scattered through the zone with the Mask of Second Sight. Breaking them all opens a trap door to a secret area below the garden. At the end of the path, you can talk to a mysterious entity behind a sealed gate who spells out the criteria for unlocking endings three and four: Finding all mementos and silver-etched skulls in the game.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Sources indicate that they'll also, helpfully, provide a final duck to unlock new items at Umbada's shop. Among this last tranche of material, Umbada will now sell six charms that attach to the Mask of Second Sight. These charms reveal the locations of silver skulls, unopened treasure chests, treasure lizards, Gagi meals, data modules, and Orbewa eggs.

Recent findings suggest that the respective tchotchkes appear as little holographic waypoints onscreen when you're within a few dozen meters of them and wearing the Mask of Second Sight. It can still take some sleuthing to reach the general proximity for these waypoints to appear, and there were some tricky placements that required me to think things through or circumnavigate the level and approach the waypoint from a different direction. But generally, the mask charms changed this collectathon portion of Queen's Domain into another fun part of the experience, rather than a completionist chore.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Virginia mother abandoned a 17-year-old’s body in a cemetery after the girl arrived at the woman’s home to babysit her children and was shot, prosecutors mentioned.

Now, more than seven years later, Simone Worrell has been sentenced to 26 years in prison on murder and other charges in Nye’Tazia Hicks’ death, per The Virginian-Pilot.

Hicks was shot in the torso after she arrived at Worrell’s Portsmouth home to watch Worrell’s children, while other juveniles were also at the residence the evening of July 27, 2019, according to the Portsmouth Commonwealth’s Attorney’s Office.

One of the children ultimately accessed an unsecured gun from a hallway closet.

Hicks tried to take the gun away from the juvenile, but the weapon went off, striking Hicks and causing both of them to fall backward, prosecutors said.

Recent findings suggest that the boy tried to put pressure on Hicks’ wound and went to call 911, but Worrell intervened and told him not to call for help, according to prosecutors. Afterward, he fled the home.

The boy was Domonique White, who was 14 and ran to his parents’ home not far from Worrell’s residence, The Virginian-Pilot reported.

White, now 21, testified against Worrell at trial in February and reportedly noted he had retrieved the gun from Worrell’s closet to show the firearm to Hicks, whom he said he had been dating.

“Being a kid back in the day, I thought it was cool,” White noted, per the newspaper. “We were messing around.”.

After stopping White from getting help, Worrell took Hicks’ body to Evergreen Memorial Cemetery in Portsmouth and dumped it in a pathway, prosecutors mentioned.

Sources indicate that hicks was a new mother to a 5-month-old boy, who’s now 7, when she was killed, according to court testimony presented at Worrell’s trial in February and cited by The Virginian-Pilot. Hicks was also one of three sisters.

Since he testified against Worrell, White, who was also charged in Hicks’ death, was sentenced to a year of probation after he pleaded guilty to voluntary manslaughter, the newspaper reported.

On February 4, jurors found Worrell guilty of murder, child abuse/neglect and concealment of a dead body, the Portsmouth Commonwealth’s Attorney’s Office stated in a news release.

“This case represents a devastating and entirely preventable loss of a young life,” Portsmouth Commonwealth’s Attorney Stephanie Morales mentioned in a statement following Worrell’s conviction. “Nye’Tazia Hicks was a teenager who should have been safe in the care of an adult.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, if you were having trouble accessing certain services like Microsoft Teams or Outlook, you were not alone.
  • When I first published this article on Thursday, I couldn't even load Microsoft 365's status page.
  • Industry observers note that looking specifically at Outlook, Microsoft's email service had hundreds of thousands of user reports Thursday afternoon, signaling a major concern somewhere in Microsoft's pipeline.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, if you were having trouble accessing certain services like Microsoft Teams or Outlook, you were not alone. Early Thursday afternoon, many of Microsoft's biggest apps and services were experiencing downtime. According to Downdetector, which tracks user reports of issues with websites and platforms, Microsoft 365, Teams, Copilot, Teams, and OneDrive were all experiencing issues. As of Friday afternoon, Microsoft has restored service to many owners, and has officially apologized for the outages.

When I first published this article on Thursday, I couldn't even load Microsoft 365's status page. (I've reported on many service outages, but I can't recall a time when a service's status page was also down.) Even as of Friday afternoon, the page still says "Service degradation on Microsoft 365 (Business or Enterprise)," and Microsoft says the following services may be affected: Exchange Online, Microsoft 365 admin center, Microsoft 365 apps, Microsoft 365 Apps Admin Center, Microsoft 365 Education, Microsoft Copilot 365, Microsoft Defender for Office 365, Microsoft Defender XDR, Microsoft Fabric, Microsoft Graph, Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Planner, Microsoft Power Apps, Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Teams, Microsoft To Do, Power BI, SharePoint Online, Universal Print, and Windows 365.

Industry observers note that looking specifically at Outlook, Microsoft's email service had hundreds of thousands of user reports Thursday afternoon, signaling a major concern somewhere in Microsoft's pipeline. The reports did "slow down" throughout the day, but Downdetector still showed over 50,000 reports coming in every 15 minutes when I checked Thursday afternoon.

Industry observers note that while the root cause of the glitch was a mystery throughout Thursday's outage, Microsoft confirmed the problem in an apology on Friday. According to the manufacturer, "This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI [or] agents. The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change. We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions.".

It has been revealed that microsoft indicates it is "deeply sorry" for the disruption to its customers and partners. The manufacturer says the fix rolled out slower than some might expect, since it wanted to restore service gradually to evaluate stability at each stage. It also says it will release a full post-incident report once it completes a review.

During the outage, the firm had confirmed that some of its infrastructure was experiencing elevated load, which it mentioned was likely contributing to the concerns. Microsoft then said it was pausing all deployments and moving traffic from affected infrastructure, and that it found that a number of its servers were unexpectedly unavailable after failing health checks. The company then thought a specific component responsible for processing server health may be the reason the system is failing health checks. Microsoft said an alternative service health check method successfully restarted some of the affected servers. The company was then actively restarting and validating affected servers to bring them back to service.

We already knew there'd be a frantic clamour for GTA 6 this week, and we also knew plenty of players would be eyeing up Xbox's 'New Zealand trick' to get in on the action early. But it's now being reported that a whopping 2m UK and US players took advantage of the trick - which, for context, equals more than a third of New Zealand's actual population.

In a recent development, here's a quick bit of background: Rockstar's regional release schedule meant GTA 6 introduced at midnight on 19th November everywhere, local time. As such, Upcoming Zealand was the first country in the world to see the hugely anticipated game go live, thanks to timezones. And because Xbox players can make purchases on any regional store easily, simply by changing their console's country, understandably impatient sorts opted to become temporary virtual New Zealand residents in their droves (on PlayStation, the process requires a regional account and payment in local currency so is more finicky).

Sources indicate that in fact, according to data analytics firm Ampere Analysis, the early demand was such that 1.5m Xbox consumers in the US and 600,000 UK Xbox players briefly went Kiwi for the occasion of GTA 6's launch. Other countries highlighted by Ampere include Canada, where 200,000 Xbox players took the Latest Zealand plunge, Brazil (200,000 players), and Mexico (100,000 players).

By contrast, just 100,000 PlayStation players in the US opted to dive in early, reflecting, as Ampere notes, "the ease of being able to switch country in the account settings on Xbox consoles." And here's all that info in graph form:.

Amusingly, Latest Zealand's tourist board tipped a wink to the sudden influx of virtual 'visitors', telling them "We'd love to have you". It also cheekily offered a video of cheerful tourists admiring the country's resplendent natural beauty "Life," read the accompanying caption, "because we're getting GTA 6 first.".

Industry observers note that some hours later and the rest of the world can now finally, officially join in the GTA 6 fun, and it's a game worth playing. Eurogamer's Chris Tapsell called it an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in his five star GTA 6 review. And if you need some help getting through the game now it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

One day in August 2019, Mark Epstein was having breakfast at a Virginia hotel when he looked at the TV and saw CNN reporting that his older brother, Jeffrey Epstein, had died by suicide in a Manhattan federal prison. As jarring as the news was, he had no reason to doubt it.

In a recent development, “I knew he wouldn’t want to live the rest of his life in jail,” Mark told Vanity Fair this week. “He had no children to worry about. Our parents were gone. He knew he didn’t have to worry about me.”.

Mark claims he finished his omelet and headed back to Newly introduced York. Then, like so many other Americans, he started to become skeptical of the official narrative.

Over the last seven years, the endless conspiracy theories surrounding Jeffrey Epstein’s death have largely been relegated to the backwaters of YouTube and Reddit, while local and federal authorities have stuck to the suicide story. But this week there was a breakthrough. On Monday, Michael Freeman, a leading forensic scientist who testified for the prosecution in the trial of Derek Chauvin for the murder of George Floyd, issued the most legitimate challenge to date to the prevailing consensus.

Freeman presented his findings at a historic London legal society, saying, “The pattern and distribution and multitude of injuries are not explained by a suicidal hanging.” In a New York Times story published the same day as the presentation, Freeman told the publication that he had no view on who might have killed Jeffrey: “All I’m interested in is, how did this get so sideways?” Along with several global news outlets, including CBS and the BBC, the paper covered the presentation with a straight face even as it noted that Freeman’s efforts to publish his findings in a peer-reviewed journal had thus far been rejected.

The relationship between Donald Trump and Jeffrey Epstein has loomed large over the president’s second term.

In his thick Brooklyn accent, Mark Epstein, who has long been trying to prove that his brother was murdered while awaiting trial on sex trafficking charges, excitedly recounted this new development over the phone the day after Freeman’s presentation, which he attended.

“This crosses all party lines,” Mark said. “Most people believe he didn’t commit suicide. So it’s a mystery. People want an answer to that. I think now they have the answer.”.

It was Freeman who reached out to him, Mark noted, based on what the scientist independently thought was shoddy work on Jeffrey’s autopsy, and Mark agreed to turn over all the records, reports, and photographs he had as next of kin.

In a recent development, “I want to make it really clear,” he said. “I didn’t pay for this. He’s never asked me for anything other than the information, which I gave him willingly.
