📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, video game consoles are more expensive than ever, but sales are growing regardless, at least in the US.
  • Video game consoles are more expensive than ever, but sales are growing regardless, at least in the US.
  • Recent findings suggest that circana has released its report for US video game industry sales in October, confirming that PS5 unit sales increased by 5% compared to October 2025.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, video game consoles are more expensive than ever, but sales are growing regardless, at least in the US. Circana has released its report for US video game industry sales in October, confirming that PS5 unit sales increased by 5% compared to October 2025. That's despite the average selling price of a PS5 increasing by 13%. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4FatSqS3VYY Xbox Series X|S unit sales jumped by 10% in October 2026 compared to October 2025, and the average selling price rose by 29% year-over-year. The Switch 2 was October 2026's top console in unit and dollar sales, and it remains 2026's best-performing console by those measurements, followed by PS5. However, Circana did not break out the specifics for Switch 2 unit sales or average selling price changes. Total hardware spending in the US on game consoles was up by 2%, reaching $357 million. Higher pricing drove the dollar sales growth, Circana mentioned, noting that PS5 dollar sales rose by 20% and Xbox Series X|S jumped by 42%. However, Switch 2 sales, measured by dollar sales, fell by 11%. Looking back to September 2026, PS5 hardware dollar sales grew by 43%, while spending on Xbox Series X|S dropped by 2% and Switch 2 fell by 12%. It will be interesting to see the November US hardware data when it comes in, as experts have said the PS5 and Xbox Series X|S could get a jolt in sales from people buying systems to play GTA 6. However, Circana has warned that sales might not be as strong as expected due to the increased prices. Microsoft, Sony, and Nintendo have raised prices on their consoles due in part to the ongoing memory and component shortages from the AI buildout. Tariffs have also played a role. On the subject of tariffs, all three received refunds from the government after the Supreme Court deemed the tariffs illegal, but those companies are keeping the money and not giving anything back to you. The companies argued that people who paid more knew what they were doing and don't deserve to get any money back.

Robert Pattinson Is the Fresh James Bond—Revisit 007’s Style Legacy Here

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1536 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There must be no male character across film history who has done more for menswear—and for the suit—than Bond, James Bond.
  • That is in part because the sartorial premise of Bond, the suave British spy, is remarkably simple: Presumably, all it takes to embody 007 is a black tuxedo, a sexy watch, and a pair of well-buffed dress shoes.
  • Recent findings suggest that denis Villeneuve is set to direct the next era of the franchise, now under the creative control of Amazon MGM, and Robert Pattinson has been chosen to reincarnate the character conceived by Ian Fleming in 1953.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There must be no male character across film history who has done more for menswear—and for the suit—than Bond, James Bond.

That is in part because the sartorial premise of Bond, the suave British spy, is remarkably simple: Presumably, all it takes to embody 007 is a black tuxedo, a sexy watch, and a pair of well-buffed dress shoes. And yet, as Daniel Craig, Pierce Brosnan, Sean Connery, and other dangerously handsome men have proven, a mere suit does not a 007 make. This is why, despite Bond being one of the most popular film characters of all time, you will rarely see ordinary men dare to take him on as a Halloween costume. There’s simply more to making Bond than a good tux.

Recent findings suggest that denis Villeneuve is set to direct the next era of the franchise, now under the creative control of Amazon MGM, and Robert Pattinson has been chosen to reincarnate the character conceived by Ian Fleming in 1953. In the announcement clip for Pattinson’s casting, the actor looks the part in a black tuxedo and white shirt, but it’s his eyes, which pierce through the camera rather than down the barrel of his gun, that do most of the talking and offer a suggestion of what Pattinson’s Bond may have to offer. Will he be a little darker and tortured, like his take on Batman? Or perhaps his Bond will be louche and somewhat pricklier.

Sources indicate that A safer bet to make is that he will look good. One of the most enduring legacies of the James Bond franchise is how stylish both the character of Bond and the universe built around him have always been. Bond has appeared classic and timeless in style during each of the franchise’s eras, but hindsight offers a much richer perspective.

Pierce Brosnan, The World Is Not Enough, 1999.

Daniel Craig, Casino Royale, 2006.

According to recent reports, as portrayed through the decades in the property’s famous title sequence, Bond is a silhouette—a classic, timeless silhouette. Fleming established the look in his development of the character when he made the suit his primary uniform. But it is Terence Young, the director of the first 007 films, who is responsible for the visual definition of Bond.

Recent findings suggest that when Connery was cast as Bond for the first film, Dr. No (1962), Young, an avid wearer of suits himself, took him to his own tailor, Anthony Sinclair. We can credit Sinclair with developing the original silver screen Bond look: The suit was lighter in fit and tailoring than most other English suits at the time. The Bond suit had a soft shoulder and waist, but a strong, wide chest and a low button stance that elongated its wearer. Every Bond suit that’s followed has been measured to the standard of Sinclair’s work, and every Bond actor has had to compete with Connery’s charisma while wearing it.

Roger Moore, The Spy Who Loved Me, 1977.

According to recent reports, brosnan and his Brioni suits were indicative of the 1990s corporate look of the time. Craig wore Brioni too, but only for Casino Royale; Tom Ford created his subsequent suiting, which often stood out for the slim fit popular in the 2010s. Most memorable sartorially is Roger Moore’s take through the ’70s and ’80s, which often deviated from the sleekness that had come to define Bond by creating a little frisson with lighter, brighter fabrics and a bolder sense of playfulness.

The character of Bond, and the actor personifying him at a given time, have also become representative of a certain male standard: Connery in the ’60s, tan and athletic, or Brosnan in the ’90s, polished with lithe elegance. And then came Craig, whose casting was met with skepticism, to put it lightly. His arrival was marked by the image of the actor walking out of the ocean in tight swim trunks in Casino Royale. His strong legs, rounded shoulders, and sculpted, hairless chest cemented then and there the idea of what a leading man had become and would look like for the next two decades.

Daniel Craig as James Bond, Casino Royale, 2006.

Industry observers note that also synonymous with Bond are his watch and many vehicles. Most recently, Bond cars have all been made by Aston Martin, though Brosnan drove some spectacular BMWs. The official Bond timepiece since Brosnan’s turn has been Omega. But before such kinds of commercial partnerships were commonplace in Hollywood, Connery wore watches by Rolex, Gruen, and Breitling, while Moore wore pieces by Seiko.

With the news that Pattinson is taking on the mantle, an equally pressing question emerges: Who will be the first new Bond girl?

According to recent reports, some of the most memorable moments in the franchise’s history have been anchored by women. Halle Berry’s emergence from the ocean in an orange bikini and a white belt safekeeping a knife was only made better by the fact that this moment was an homage to the first Bond girl, Ursula Andress, and her ivory two-piece featuring a belt for her own weapon. Then there was Eva Green as Vesper Lynd in a slinky Versace dress in Casino Royale. But it didn’t get better than Grace Jones in A View to a Kill. As May Day, a fabulous femme fatale, Jones wore costumes designed for her by Azzedine Alaïa. How could anyone measure up?

Halle Berry and Pierce Brosnan, Die Another Day, 2002.

Roger Moore and Grace Jones, 1985, A View To a Kill, 1985.

Of course, we will have to see how stylistic choices play out in the 26th Bond film, which, like Bond movies of the past, will become emblematic of the era in which we live. It will also, as a creative project, have to contend with the way Hollywood operates today. The fact that Amazon now has full creative control over the franchise—the organization acquired MGM, a co-owner of the Bond franchise rights, for $8.45 billion in 2022 and later struck a deal with the other co-owners in regard to creative authority—is the primary indication of that.

Pattinson will also be the first Bond with airtight fashion-brand deals. Craig was an Omega ambassador as an extension of his role as Bond, which made him a household name, and the 007s who came before him operated within a film industry that was not as closely connected to fashion.

In a recent development, also unlike his predecessors, Pattinson is stepping into the role as a bona fide movie star who has appeared in three other major franchises (Harry Potter, Twilight, and Batman). He’s already one of the most prolific and bankable stars of his generation, and an undeniable part of being a movie star today is becoming the face of a franchise, a brand, or a product.

In September, Pattinson was announced as a global ambassador for Jaeger-LeCoultre, a Swiss watchmaker. But 007 has worn Omega watches onscreen for decades, a partnership between the brand and the franchise that dates back to the Brosnan years. If Omega’s partnership with the franchise remains for this upcoming installment, it could present a potential conflict if Pattinson’s contract with Jaeger stipulates that he is not allowed to wear another brand’s watch onscreen or front related campaigns for competitors. It may sound like a banal preoccupation, as Pattinson has only just been cast, but there are millions of dollars at play, and actors today often make as much money from brand deals as they do from their turns onscreen.

In a recent development, pattinson has also been an ambassador for Dior since 2013, serving first as a fragrance ambassador and subsequently as a face for ready-to-wear Dior Homme; he was originally tapped under Kris Van Assche, with his ambassadorship extending through Kim Jones’s tenure at the renamed Dior Men and now continuing with Jonathan Anderson at the helm of the French mega-brand. Will Anderson be providing his suits? The Irish designer has costumed films before, working with Luca Guadagnino on Challengers, Queer, and the upcoming Artificial. To design for the big screen would hardly be a stretch for him.

According to recent reports, the real question is more existential: Should Bond wear high fashion? To return to the idea of the 007 silhouette, that in itself is counterintuitive to Pattinson saving the world in one of Anderson’s menswear takes on the famous Dior Bar jacket, with its nipped waist and slightly flared hem. And yet in this brave upcoming world of brand deals, anything is possible.

Mysterious GTA 6 leaker Cyberleek has reemerged in the wake of GTA 6's release with another leak: This time, they have released what they claim to be a near-complete build of GTA 6 on Xbox from November 2026.

In their post, Cyberleek states they'll drop the one file they've withheld—the main executable—if their crypto coin reaches a $15 million market cap. Yeah, we're doing this again. Comments on a now-removed Reddit post say the leaked file is around 200 GB, which is close to the size of GTA 6 on consoles.

Cyberleek claims they will release the exe on November 23, no matter what.

"It is an Xbox build this time, not a PC build. CL does not care. This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps. CL told you not to preorder for a reason. This is one of the reasons," the posts read.

"If the Xbox build cannot be made to work and support holds, CL will work to get a PS5 build—a fallback, most likely never required. Either way: the Xbox build is going out. No double dipping for Take-Two/Rockstar.".

Last we heard from Cyberleek was over a month ago, when they were threatening Take-Two with a "dead man's switch", which many took to mean they'd either post major story spoilers or leak the game in its entirety.

According to recent reports, we've yet to see confirmation that the build is genuine, but that could come as soon as tonight. If it is, it'll be anywhere between a few days or hours before the executable comes: According to Cyberleek's site, their crypto right now sits at a $1.83 million cap.

Tech Report: Infamous GTA 6 leaker CyberLeek is back, and this time the group claims to have leaked a full development build of the game

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, cyberLeek, the persona of a hacker group that was responsible for leaking GTA 6 gameplay before the game introduced, has reappeared today, claiming to have released a development build of the final version of the game on its site.
  • Various social media accounts have visited the site and noted the size of the download offered by CyberLeek is, indeed 209GB.
  • "It is done," a statement from CyberLeek reads.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, cyberLeek, the persona of a hacker group that was responsible for leaking GTA 6 gameplay before the game introduced, has reappeared today, claiming to have released a development build of the final version of the game on its site. This new leak appears to be making good on a threat posted back in October, where the group stated its intent to release a full, playable build of the game.

Various social media accounts have visited the site and noted the size of the download offered by CyberLeek is, indeed 209GB. Eurogamer has seen the site and can confirm this is what the group has claimed, however I have been unable to verify the existence of any actual files. On the site, CyberLeek claims this build is from November 2026 - meaning it is very close to (if not the actual) release build. The 'executable file appears to be missing from the build, however, meaning you cannot actually - yet - get it up and running. CyberLeek is threatening to release this file at a later date, however.

"It is done," a statement from CyberLeek reads. "[Cyberleek] holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto 6, and it is going out by torrent. Now. Every file except one. The main executable is held on a countdown." CyberLeek says the executable will be released earlier than planned if its crypto token reaches a predetermined value. Many of the leaks to date have been related to a CyberLeek crypto scheme. Previously, it was estimated that the group cashed out at least £200,000.

It has been revealed that what does all this mean? There's a very realistic chance that the game could be up and running on PC soon - undercutting Rockstar's unannounced PC release by a matter of months, if current rumours are to be believed. "This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps," the statement continues. "[CyberLeek] told you not to preorder for a reason. This is one of the reasons.

Recent findings suggest that "If the Xbox build cannot be made to work and support holds, [CyberLeek] will work to get a PS5 build - a fallback, most likely never required. Either way: the Xbox build is going out. No double dipping for Take-Two/Rockstar." It seems these are not empty threats.

CyberLeek has been a thorn in Rockstar's side for a while now. The group initially claimed it took this action in the name of "Gamers' Rights", supposedly fighting for consumers in relation to the controversial discontinuation of game-discs and the digital-only future being pursued by game publishers. Rockstar has previously issued statements regarding the leaker, noting that the leaks are "heartbreaking" and that "this is obviously not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time". Take-Two tried to subpoena Discord for information pertaining to the leaker's identity.

Savannah Chrisley has something to say about the speculation she’s a “gold digger” for marrying husband Jason Galanis despite their 27-year age difference.

“The way that I live my life, I am in a very healthy, happy relationship. I don’t have chaos, I don’t have turmoil [and] I’m not wondering how I’m going to pay my bills,” Savannah, 29, told her dad, Todd Chrisley, on the Tuesday, November 17, episode of her “Unlocked” podcast. “My life is very peaceful, very calming, very just zen, OK? I love it, it’s great. So, what better situation than to bring a child into a home that is stable and loving and all the great things?”.

Savannah and Galanis, 56, started dating in 2025 before announcing last month that they are expecting a baby. The couple quietly got married in the Cayman Islands in July amid the reality TV alum’s pregnancy.

While Savannah has frequently gushed about her newlywed bliss, social media critics have branded the podcaster a gold digger over the pair’s age gap.

“Me, being a gold digger? I don’t,” she started, clapping back at the assumptions. “Sure, I have expectations, like, I am the mother of your child, you’re putting a roof over my head. You’re providing for me, but I work. I’m sitting here … and [I] had my own money.”.

She continued, “I have worked. I am sitting here seven months pregnant still doing a podcast. Yes, I do it because I love it, but also because I’m not doing it for free. I make money off of it; I have contractual obligations.”.

Todd, 57, noted that he hopes to see his daughter continue to work once her baby boy arrives. (In addition to Savannah, Todd shares sons Chase and Grayson with wife Julie Chrisley. They also adopted daughter Chloe, the biological daughter of Todd’s son Kyle from his first marriage.).

GTA 6’s Digital Release Has GameStop CEO Defending Physical Games, For Obvious Reasons

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The GTA 6 launch looks set to break several records, as the digital-only game appears on track to be a major critical and commercial hit.
  • It has been revealed that the GTA 6 launch looks set to break several records, as the digital-only game appears on track to be a major critical and commercial hit.
  • Sources indicate that "When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it, or lend it to a friend," Cohen mentioned to Bloomberg.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The GTA 6 launch looks set to break several records, as the digital-only game appears on track to be a major critical and commercial hit. Right on cue, GameStop CEO Ryan Cohen has criticized publishers that forgo a traditional physical release as a business strategy that hurts consumers and GameStop's bottom line, without explicitly mentioning GTA 6 publisher Take-Two Interactive. "When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it, or lend it to a friend," Cohen remarked to Bloomberg. "Unquestionably, the decision to move to all-digital has hurt consumers, and it's also hurt GameStop. Of course they don't like [trade-ins] because removing a used copy eliminates an alternative to buying new. They're taking away competition." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RQvBOySNq1U Cohen's comments come in the wake of GTA 6 being a digital-only release--the "physical" edition includes a download code for it. It's also somewhat ironic for Cohen to defend physical games, given the GameStop boss's July remarks that physical video games were "irrelevant" to GameStop's business strategy. That business model has relied heavily on secondhand game sales, and none of those profits ever made their way back to the original publishers. Presently, GameStop states that selling video game software makes up the smallest part of its business. But in the case of GTA 6? Going digital probably made financial sense for Take-Two Interactive and developer Rockstar Games. The entire game clocks in at over 211GB, which means three standard 100GB Ultra HD Blu-ray discs would have been needed to house GTA 6 in its launch-day entirety--although realistically, Take-Two probably would have opted for one disc and forced consumers to download the rest of the game. That would have raised costs, and it wouldn't be unlikely to imagine Take-Two fearing the discs being reverse-engineered for secrets ahead of GTA 6's launch. Going digital essentially removed those risks, and while PlayStation and Xbox do take a cut of profits for hosting the game on their servers. According to Sensor Tower, GTA 6 sales for PS5 alone have reached $1.38 billion in revenue so far, which means Sony is profiting handsomely from those sales. Retailers are still entitled to a share of the profits for stocking the code-in-a-box version of the game on their shelves, and once you start to factor in distribution costs, Take-Two's reasoning starts to make sense. The publisher says 98% of its business is digital, but it's not ruling out a proper physical GTA 6 edition in the future. For more on GTA 6, from completing side missions to finding a tricky location on the sprawling map of Leonida, we’ve got you covered with our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

Tech Report: Steven Spielberg Gently Pitched Christopher Nolan The Movie Idea I Think Fans Have Been Wanting

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (661 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cinemablend

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that I don't know how you follow a $1.8 billion trip through Greek mythology, but Steven Spielberg apparently has an idea.
  • It has been revealed that the moment came Tuesday, Nov.
  • The only other thing I want to say, not to challenge you or anything, but there’s always The Iliad.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that I don't know how you follow a $1.8 billion trip through Greek mythology, but Steven Spielberg apparently has an idea. Christopher Nolan is still taking a victory lap for The Odyssey, one of the biggest hits on the 2026 movie schedule, and the Jaws director just floated a follow-up I'd pay good money to see. The way he brought it up made me laugh, too. Even Hollywood legends know how to suggest another movie without sounding too pushy.

It has been revealed that the moment came Tuesday, Nov. 17, at an awards-season screening of The Odyssey in Los Angeles. Spielberg moderated a Q&A with Nolan at the Directors Guild of America theater, where he praised the filmmaker's latest blockbuster before slipping in one more suggestion. As Gizmodo's Germain Lussier reported from the event, Spielberg told him:.

The only other thing I want to say, not to challenge you or anything, but there’s always The Iliad.

Sources indicate that I love how politely Spielberg slid that into the conversation. It's the cinematic equivalent of complimenting somebody's enormous Thanksgiving dinner and then asking what they're making next year. He even followed it up by insisting there was no pressure. Nolan, understandably, joked that Spielberg seemed to be speaking for Universal Pictures. Spielberg admitted the studio would probably appreciate it, but he was interested himself.

According to recent reports, the idea makes a lot of sense. Homer's The Iliad takes place during the Trojan War, before Odysseus spends years trying to get home in The Odyssey. It wouldn't be a straightforward sequel, since we'd be going backward in the timeline, but the stories share a world. Imagine Nolan using his massive practical sets and IMAX cameras to tackle the conflict between Achilles and Hector. I'm already looking for a seat.

Sources indicate that here's what really makes the suggestion fun: Nolan almost got his shot at The Iliad decades ago. He was originally hired to direct Troy, the 2004 movie that eventually went to Wolfgang Petersen and starred Brad Pitt as Achilles. Nolan has since explained that he carried ideas from that unrealized project into The Odyssey, including the impressive Trojan Horse sequence.

Nolan has already explained why he chose The Odyssey. He considers The Iliad more grounded, while the later poem's monsters and stranger adventures offered something he hadn't seen done the way he envisioned. That doesn't mean he couldn't change his mind, especially after his latest movie has reportedly earned more than $1.8 billion worldwide.

Recent findings suggest that there's also something delightful about Spielberg being the person to make this pitch. He helped develop Interstellar before Nolan took over, and Nolan consulted him while preparing Dunkirk. Watching Spielberg praise Nolan as a fellow filmmaker and then immediately ask for another movie feels like the most recognizable fan behavior imaginable.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

For now, Nolan hasn't confirmed his next directing project. He told the crowd that he tends to focus on one film at a time and figures out the next one only after he's finished. So nobody should start booking tickets for The Iliad just yet. But if the man who gave us Jaws, Raiders of the Lost Ark, and Jurassic Park is personally asking for another giant Homer adaptation, I think somebody at Universal should at least write that suggestion down. Maybe keep the IMAX cameras handy.

In the meantime, The Odyssey is now available to rent or buy digitally, as well as on Blu-ray and 4K Blu-ray.

Industry News: 10 Privacy Hacks Every Mac User Should Know

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1060 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that apple has a pretty good track record on privacy.
  • In a recent development, enabling the macOS Firewall (which is off by default) adds a layer of protection against external devices on your wifi network, as well as unauthorized apps from initiating a connection to your device.
  • Recent findings suggest that another hack for maintaining privacy on public networks is to enable rotating MAC addresses, which randomizes the identifier your device broadcasts when scanning for and connecting to wifi.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that apple has a pretty good track record on privacy. The company bakes a number of protections into its OSes to keep your data from being shared or stolen. That said, you can make your Apple devices even more secure. There are plenty of opt-in settings that make it even harder for anyone to snoop on your device and activity. These are the best privacy hacks for your Mac.

In a recent development, enabling the macOS Firewall (which is off by default) adds a layer of protection against external devices on your wifi network, as well as unauthorized apps from initiating a connection to your device. Turning on Stealth Mode prevents your Mac from even responding to these requests, essentially making it invisible to anything that's scanning a network you're connected to. This makes it more difficult for hackers and malware to know your device exists, much less attack it. This can interfere with certain essential activity when you're on your home network, but it's a valuable security setting when on public wifi. You can leave Firewall on all the time and enable Stealth Mode only as needed. Go to Settings > Network > Firewall, flip the toggle, then hit Options to manage Stealth Mode.

Recent findings suggest that another hack for maintaining privacy on public networks is to enable rotating MAC addresses, which randomizes the identifier your device broadcasts when scanning for and connecting to wifi. If you use either your real MAC address or a fixed one (random but unchanging), it's easier to track your activity on that network, including when you arrive, how long you stay, and when you leave. Rotating addresses are best for public, shared networks you temporarily connect to, and don't require a login via a captive portal (like hotel wifi). You can turn this on for specific networks via Settings > Wi-Fi > [Network Name] > Details and change Private Wi-Fi address to Rotating.

Images and screenshots contain metadata, such as timestamps, device and hardware details, and, in the case of photos, physical location. Much of this information is stripped automatically when you share files to social media or via encrypted messaging apps, but if you're sending them via text or email, posting to forums, or sharing over AirDrop, metadata remains intact. You can easily remove metadata from your images right on your desktop. Select the file and hit control + click to bring up an options menu, then go to Quick Actions > Convert Image. Uncheck the box next to Preserve Metadata, then hit Convert. (This is also useful for swiftly converting HEIC to JPEG without opening a separate app.).

It has been revealed that apple collects information about your device for diagnostic purposes or to improve apps and services, some of which is shared with third-party app developers. This may include crash and usage data as well as recordings and transcripts of Siri interactions and iCloud analytics. You can disable sharing for some or all of these categories under Settings > Privacy & Security > Analytics & Improvements.

According to recent reports, you may be surprised by the number of apps and system services that use your device's location in the background. You should definitely disable location services for third-party apps that don't require location to function. You can find these toggles under Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services. You can also turn off location permissions for some Apple apps and services if you're not using them on your device, like Weather and Maps. Finally, tap System Services and disable location for any non-essential features—at the very least, disable "Mac Analytics" and "Significant Locations & routes" (which lets your Mac and other iCloud devices learn locations and routes you use often).

In a recent development, third-party apps on your Mac that need access to your device's camera and microphone have to request permission, and it's easy to grant this in the moment and then forget that you've allowed it. You should regularly audit which apps have these permissions and revoke access from those that don't need them on a day-to-day basis. Disabling them forces the app to ask again. Go to Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone or Camera to see the allowed apps and flip the toggle to disable permissions.

Another permission type you may have granted without much thought is local network access. This allows third-party apps to discover and communicate with other devices—printers, smart speakers, and IoT devices—on your home wifi. While this may be useful for services like Spotify that cast to connected hardware, other utilities, media apps, and games probably don't need to be mapping your network in the background. Go to Settings > Privacy & Security > Local Network to audit permissions and disable those that aren't needed.

Industry observers note that another key permission to check concerns third-party apps that have access to your Mac's full disk, which includes data from Mail, Messages, Safari, Home, Time Machine, and admin settings. If an app only works with files you explicitly open and save, it doesn't need full disk access. Legitimate use cases may include antivirus and malware scanners, productivity tools, or backup utilities that you trust. You can also audit which apps have access to specific files and folders. This is under Settings > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access or Files & Folders.

If you're using iCloud to store photos, files, and device backups, your data is encrypted on Apple's servers and in transit. Apple still holds the decryption key, which is useful if you somehow get locked out of your account and need help recovering it, but for sensitive data—including device backups—end-to-end encryption is the most secure way to ensure no one but you can gain access. Advanced Data Protection is an opt-in setting for iCloud that encrypts your information end to end. You'll need to set up an alternative recovery method, such as your device passcode with two-factor authentication, a recovery contact, or a recovery key. Be careful, though: If you lose access to this recovery method, you will lose your data. You can enable Advanced Data Protection on your Mac under System Settings > [Your Name] > iCloud > Advanced Data Protection > Turn On. Note that some iCloud data, including passwords and payment methods, are already end-to-end encrypted by default.

Why GTA 6 Doesn’t Include Disney World

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (668 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Walt Disney World is synonymous with Florida, but the iconic theme park doesn't show up in Rockstar's GTA 6, which takes place in a fictional Florida called Leonida.
  • Walt Disney World is synonymous with Florida, but the iconic theme park doesn't show up in Rockstar's GTA 6, which takes place in a fictional Florida called Leonida.
  • According to recent reports, rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson mentioned the decision to came down to resources and story reasons.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Walt Disney World is synonymous with Florida, but the iconic theme park doesn't show up in Rockstar's GTA 6, which takes place in a fictional Florida called Leonida. Many are wondering why, especially when GTA: Vice City had its own parody of the theme park--Fun World--many years ago. Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson noted the decision to came down to resources and story reasons. “A theme park would represent a lot of work that we didn’t have, and we didn’t have a strong narrative reason to send them there,” he told VGC. Nelson added that Rockstar isn't known to cut corners, so if GTA 6 were to have its own version of Walt Disney World, it would be a "fully functioning theme park," and that just wasn't doable. Walt Disney World is much more than just its most famous park, Magic Kingdom. The property includes three other main parks, Animal Kingdom, Hollywood Studios, and Epcot, along with the Disney Springs shopping district, multiple water parks and golf courses, and more than two-dozen hotels. The entire property is more than 25,000 acres. Even if Rockstar were to replicate only a portion of the scale of the real Walt Disney World, it would surely be a significant job. Players might expect fully functioning rides, and Nelson said the challenge for Rockstar would be, "Where do you stop? When do you feel like it's enough?" Nelson said people think Rockstar has unlimited time and money, and that isn't true. "So sometimes you just have to admit we are not going to be able to make this to the level we feel we need to,” he said. Plus, as Nelson pointed out, there would need to be a story reason to send Jason and Lucia hundreds of miles north from Miami to Orlando, where Walt Disney World is. GTA 6 has a huge map, but it's contained to Vice City and its surrounding areas--it doesn't go that far north.

#51255. Industry News: Ubisoft says Assassin's Creed Jade is still alive as it merges two of its Creative Houses

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (658 w)
📖 Baca

Industry News: Ubisoft says Assassin's Creed Jade is still alive as it merges two of its Creative Houses

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (658 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ubisoft has confirmed that while Assassin's Creed Jade - its mobile entry in the series - is still in development, its focus remains with console and PC.
  • Speaking during the earnings call for Ubisoft's first-half results, CFO Frédérick Duguet said mobile was "still an opportunity for the medium to longer term, with games such as AC Jade on Assassin’s Creed", according to a transcript of the call published by Investing.com.
  • According to recent reports, "Looking at what we can see in terms of long-term financial return, in the mindset of having a stronger focus in terms of capital allocation and financial returns, we consider that we would rather put our resources on bigger opportunities," Duguet said.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubisoft has confirmed that while Assassin's Creed Jade - its mobile entry in the series - is still in development, its focus remains with console and PC.

Speaking during the earnings call for Ubisoft's first-half results, CFO Frédérick Duguet said mobile was "still an opportunity for the medium to longer term, with games such as AC Jade on Assassin’s Creed", according to a transcript of the call published by Investing.com.

According to recent reports, "Looking at what we can see in terms of long-term financial return, in the mindset of having a stronger focus in terms of capital allocation and financial returns, we consider that we would rather put our resources on bigger opportunities," Duguet said. "Today, we can say that console and PC remain our core focus for our biggest franchises.".

He added: "The focus is really to make sure that we come with strong growth on console and PC, and notably PC, which is a more dynamic platform than ever.".

Ubisoft last confirmed its China-set mobile game was still in the works in March, when it was mentioned in the publisher’s Assassin's Creed: Into 2026 blog. Assassin's Creed now sits within Vantage Studios, Ubisoft's joint venture with Tencent, which introduced last year.

Recent findings suggest that ubisoft's results also confirmed some more changes to the way the organization is run, with the publisher saying its upcoming operating model is "now fully in place". Creative Houses 3 and 5 have been combined under the leadership of Julien Bares "to leverage synergies between Live experiences across platforms".

In a recent development, all leadership roles across the Creative Houses are now filled, too. An external general manager has been appointed for Creative House 4 and is set to join in January 2027, though Ubisoft hasn't yet confirmed who. That follows September's appointment of 2K and Amazon Games veteran Christoph Hartmann to lead Creative House 2, home to The Division, Ghost Recon, and Splinter Cell, which was renamed Massive Entertainment at the same time.

Outside the Creative Houses, Motherbrain, the team behind Ubisoft's generative AI experiment Teammates, is now a subsidiary in its own right. It's working on "smart NPCs with memory and AI game masters that manage large-scale systemic worlds". A separate unit has also been set up to look after brands that don't belong to any of the Creative Houses.

Ubisoft claims the fresh structure is already paying off, pointing to the commercial success of Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced and renewed momentum for Rainbow Six Siege, which it says ranked among the top 10 games across Xbox and PlayStation for monthly active people over the half.

That mentioned, the publisher nonetheless posted a net loss of €254.5 million for the first half of the year, with net bookings down 16.5 percent to €644.7 million.

Recent findings suggest that the news comes just hours after Ubisoft confirmed 166 job cuts at its Montréal and Québec City studios, the latest in a year of layoffs. They're part of the "major organisational, operational and portfolio reset" that Ubisoft announced in January. That initial announcement was accompanied by the news of two studio closures - affecting its Halifax mobile and Stockholm teams - plus the cancellation of six projects, including the much-delayed Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time remake.

In a recent development, since then, 105 jobs have been cut at Red Storm Entertainment, the Ubisoft studio behind the Ghost Recon series, and around 380 employees were reportedly laid off when the publisher's Winnipeg and Belgrade teams shut in June. In October, Ubisoft closed Trials developer RedLynx and downsized its Singapore Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced team, impacting a total of approximately 120 employees. Amid all this, Ubisoft developers have been on strike in response to the publisher's sweeping layoffs.

On the weekend, we learned that Ubisoft is reportedly working on a fresh Rainbow Six Vegas game 18 years after the last entry in the series.

#51253. Pedro Almodóvar Didn’t Think He Could Write a Novel. But Once He Started, the “Story Began to Pour Out”

Pedro Almodóvar Didn’t Think He Could Write a Novel. But Once He Started, the “Story Began to Pour Out”

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 19 min read (3841 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~19 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, A woman who might, or might not, be Penélope Cruz stares down at us from the wall.
  • Industry observers note that this brings to mind one of the stories in Almodóvar’s first novel, The Man Who Only Wrote on Airplanes.
  • Sources indicate that both works have much in common: They are works of autofiction with protagonists—the filmmakers played by Bárbara Lennie and Leonardo Sbaraglia in the film, and a very multifaceted character named Flavio Guijarro in the book—who appear to be alternative versions of their creator.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A woman who might, or might not, be Penélope Cruz stares down at us from the wall. For now, I’ll accept that it is Cruz because the image is on a poster for Broken Embraces, a 2009 film she starred in. My hesitation in believing it’s her, however, is because finding a resemblance between the woman on the poster and Cruz requires a lot of generosity. It’s as if the artist had painted her based on a detailed description he’d heard, but he’d never actually seen his subject onscreen. “We were given this in India,” explains Pedro Almodóvar’s brother, Agustín, the head and owner of El Deseo, the production company behind Almodóvar’s films. “Specialized artists still hand-paint their movie posters, and the results are images like this.” The work’s imperfections give it a charm that no poster created by AI could ever match.

Industry observers note that this brings to mind one of the stories in Almodóvar’s first novel, The Man Who Only Wrote on Airplanes. It depicts a Blade Runner–style dystopian future where replicants, jaded by digital perfection, are fascinated by the rough edges of human culture. The book has just been published in Spain (it is scheduled to be published in the United States, in Spanish, in February 2027), following the release of Almodóvar’s latest film, Bitter Christmas (which will be in select US theaters on November 13, and released nationwide on November 25).

Sources indicate that both works have much in common: They are works of autofiction with protagonists—the filmmakers played by Bárbara Lennie and Leonardo Sbaraglia in the film, and a very multifaceted character named Flavio Guijarro in the book—who appear to be alternative versions of their creator. At the same time, they are clearly different from Almodóvar, like the difference between Cruz and the woman on the Indian movie poster.

I ask Almodóvar why he decided to recount Flavio’s story in the form of a novel rather than a movie, but he appears to have not heard my question and answers instead as if I’d asked him why it took him so long to publish a novel, which is undoubtedly much more interesting: “I think the reason I hadn’t written a novel until now was that I wasn’t sure I’d be able to, even though I’d wanted to write one since I was a young man. At first, however, I didn’t even know myself that this story would be a novel. I started with a simple anecdote about an acting coach and an actor, and that opened the floodgates; the story began to pour out. When it was already over 30 pages, I sent it to my editor. He told me there was a novel there and that I should keep going.”.

The 77-year-old director from La Mancha poses in a jacket, polo shirt, pants, and sneakers by Loewe.

He will answer many other questions that I haven’t asked but should have: “I didn’t know, for example, that I’d include my story ‘Addiction,’ which is a little treat for fans that had already appeared in Pain and Glory. It was going to be a monologue that Carmen Machi would perform in a small theater, but I ended up giving it to Asier Etxeandia in that film. I also wrote Pain and Glory very promptly. And in it, I inserted, like little snippets, more pieces that I’d already written. For example, there’s another story, just five pages long, about a chance encounter with an actor with whom I’d had a very bad relationship in the past [Eusebio Poncela, who starred in Law of Desire 40 years ago] and with whom, in the story, I ended up doing heroin. In real life, the fact that he was using heroin while we were filming was the reason we had a falling out. Thanks to those preexisting elements, which fit into the story, I was able to write that movie so quickly. And the same is true of my new book. What defines it is a sense of absolute freedom.”.

And maybe that sentence is, in the end, the answer to all my questions for Almodóvar.

Vanity Fair España: Is that sense of freedom why you decided to write a novel instead of a screenplay?

Pedro Almodóvar: In Bitter Christmas, Leonardo Sbaraglia’s character indicates he needs absolute freedom to work. Just like me throughout my entire career. That freedom feels more intense with a novel because it’s a format with which I have less experience. I’ve woven it together from different stories, but they all revolve around the protagonist and it’s been very satisfying. It wasn’t a whim: The book has the same rigor to it as everything else I do, but that freedom is deeply rooted in my style. That’s why I wrote it so quickly. Everything flowed naturally.

According to recent reports, there is a tradition of using a novel as a container for many stories, as with Don Quixote or Jan Potocki’s The Manuscript Found in Saragossa. On the other hand, speaking of influences, it’s interesting that when you wrote your Patty Diphusa stories in 1983 [included in Patty Diphusa and Other Writings, published by Faber & Faber in 1992], Anita Loos and pornographic photo novels are influences that appear in the mix, but in The Man Who Only Wrote on Airplanes, you turn to, let’s say, more distinguished names: Henry James, Nabokov, and Colm Tóibín, who even appears as a character.

It has been revealed that I’m not trying to compare myself to Cervantes or Potocki, but yes, that’s what the book is. That’s precisely why this novel can’t be adapted for the screen: You’d have to choose one part of it and develop it, but as it stands now, that wouldn’t be possible. Those earlier influences are still with me—Anita Loos is certainly among them—and they continue to inspire me with both specific phrases and broader themes. In the novel, I name authors who inspire me and with whom I connect organically, such as Joan Didion and Virginia Woolf. But Patty and Flavio have something in common: a sense of urgency that drives them to write at a breakneck pace, out of a physiological need. Neither of them sleeps much, though in Patty’s case it’s because she can’t stop doing cocaine. Beyond that, other differences set them apart, including the differences between what life was like in the ’80s and what it’s like now.

What sort of differences are there, and where are they most apparent?

Sources indicate that take sex, for example. Patty Diphusa is an archetype of the 1980s, a time of absolute freedom in Spain, and her character can only be understood in the context of the utterly carefree and hedonistic lifestyle we led back then. If she sucks a guy's dick in a bathroom, she’ll then record her wild thoughts because she considers herself a sort of philosopher of eroticism. Although Flavio is a very free-spirited person, just like the book itself, he belongs to another era and another generation. Here, sex is part of a love story, and his attitude toward it is very different. I devote less space to the erotic scenes in this book because I assume people already know what it’s like to sleep with someone.

Almodóvar, in another room at El Deseo’s headquarters, wearing a Louis Vuitton jacket and a Prada knit polo shirt.

You’ve argued on different occasions that in the 1980s, many people in Spain chose that hedonistic and seemingly frivolous lifestyle as a reaction to the previous era, and that this was a political statement. Now we see a latest generation adopting a different kind of stance. For example, all across Europe, people are taking to the streets to demand their right to housing and decent living conditions, and there’s not much frivolity in that. How do you interpret this change?

I completely empathize with and support the people filling the streets. They are demanding fundamental rights that are enshrined in the Spanish constitution and which are now in jeopardy: housing, health care, and education. I went to the encampment on the Puerta del Sol [in Madrid] only a few times, because I was in Fresh York presenting Bitter Christmas at the New York Film Festival and also because I think a famous person doesn’t really fit in at these demonstrations—if we go, we distort the spirit of it. But I did go, and I bought them food because that’s what I thought they’d need, even though they told me they’d be better off with some tables. I don’t just support their initiative; I’m glad it happened. One thing I’d heard about young people, a generation I don’t know much about, was from a news article that said that 25% of young Spaniards wouldn’t mind living under a dictatorship like Franco’s. I shuddered. What happened in the Puerta del Sol shows that there’s a whole crowd of young people beyond those who go to Ferraz to pray the rosary [since November 2023, a group of Catholic protesters has gathered daily to pray outside the headquarters of the PSOE, Spain’s socialist party, on Madrid’s Calle Ferraz]. They aren’t rich, and they don’t have their lives figured out; they can’t work in the professions they studied to pursue, and they don’t earn enough money to buy homes. That’s terrifying. And the political parties have shown their true colors when it comes to housing. Of course, the PSOE is late to the game with the so-called Maricarmen decrees [a series of measures named after Maricarmen Abascal, whose eviction from her home and subsequent death in October galvanized activists], but at least it has reacted. The starkly different reactions from the Partido Popular [Popular Party] and Vox [center-right and far-right parties, respectively] already tell you what they think about this matter.

Would you agree today with that line from Gloria Muñoz in The Flower of My Secret: “With so much reality, the country’s ready to explode”?

She was talking in literary terms, but it’s true that this phrase has taken on a life of its own over time and has spilled over into other areas. The same thing has happened to another phrase: “A woman is more authentic the more she resembles the person she has dreamed of becoming,” as Agrado remarked in All About My Mother. It was a line written for a transgender woman, and one that makes perfect sense for her. But now it can be understood in relation to any kind of character: It speaks to authenticity, to staying true to oneself and to one’s own dreams. In the case of young people in our country, we’re talking about a social reality. The country has changed a lot, and we’re very polarized—though France is even worse off than Spain. Europe is in very bad shape overall. The kind of news coverage being produced plays a major role in this rise of the far right. Since the images promoted by the right are so jarring and sensationalist, TV stations pick up on them, and in doing so, they’re effectively promoting figures like Vito Quiles [a far-right activist and influencer]. Damn it, don’t put Vito Quiles on TV—it’s better if we don’t even know where he is or what he’s doing!

Are you particularly concerned about the attention that the far right is getting?

Recent findings suggest that people like [Santiago] Abascal [president of the Vox political party] and [Javier]Milei [president of Argentina] want to do away with the state. Milei, the biggest loudmouth of them all, even aims to destroy the state from within the state itself, which is diabolical. I cite Milei as an example because he indicates so himself. And on top of that, people elect him for that very reason: He’s someone who has come to power democratically, just like [Donald] Trump. So we’re putting the tools of democracy in the hands of someone whose main goal is to destroy it. Furthermore, in a world so polarized—and with a far right that has no qualms about calling itself fascist—the emergence of AI creates a perfect storm.

One of the stories in your book is, in fact, a dystopian tale inspired by Blade Runner, in which large corporations with shadowy agendas seek to create a less human world. You have contributed so much to human creativity. Are you concerned about how that creativity is being taken over by AI?

In a recent development, I’m always open to change. It’s necessary for society to move forward. But I think the encroachment of AI on human agency is terrible. They should start regulating it now. I’m concerned about the jobs it will replace and also the synthetic culture it will create. In fact, a synthetic culture based on data already exists, and it lacks a soul. The genesis of a screenplay must be human, because AI doesn’t have the sense of doubt, the patience, or the capacity for stories to build up layers of meaning, as in Talk to Her and Bad Education. We need a society that cares about culture, promotes it, and supports it, and not a soulless culture focused only on the immediate. I haven’t used AI creatively, nor do I really know how to. But I’m concerned that we’re now unable to tell whether an image is real or not, given the level of perfection this technology has reached. And moreover, behind it all are very powerful people who know no limits.

Industry observers note that on another topic, standards of beauty have changed, with cosmetic surgery and fillers now widely prevalent. For someone who places such importance on the expressions of actors that must also be a cause for concern.

It has been revealed that well, I wouldn’t mind if an actor in one of my movies had had plastic surgery. For example, I wouldn’t turn down Nicole Kidman for that reason—she’s not only a great actor, but she has also had plastic surgery, and she looks better than ever. Because, these days, actors who’ve had plastic surgery are part of the landscape. It’s so common that you no longer have to explain that a character has had it done; it’s accepted as a matter of course. What’s more, cosmetic surgery has advanced so much that high-profile figures who’ve had work done—like Donatella Versace, Lindsay Lohan, or Nicole Kidman herself—have completely erased the signs of their previous procedures with splendid results. [Editor’s note: Lindsay Lohan has denied having a facelift, while Kidman has never confirmed undergoing any plastic surgery.] The major problem is that, if you make films set in the past, you can’t cast women with plastic surgery or lip fillers; it would be anachronistic, just like putting a piece of furniture from the 1980s in a film about the Spanish Civil War. But it’s true that in my films, plastic surgery hasn’t usually been an option, for aesthetic reasons. Fortunately, there will always be people like Frances McDormand and Carmen Maura. We need older women who look their age.

Sources indicate that what interests me most about your new novel is the protagonist’s relationship with an actor, Alez Mazado—a sex symbol who isn’t very intelligent but has a certain natural talent and is open to being molded. Flavio is his Pygmalion. There’s even an explicit reference to Hitchcock’s film Vertigo, which also features that kind of relationship. Do you often have that kind of dynamic with your actors?

It has been revealed that I’m like Jimmy Stewart in Vertigo: With actors, I get involved in their hair, lip color, outfits—everything. When I watched Vertigo for the umpteenth time, I thought that character was a director: “He knows exactly what he wants,” they tell him when he takes Kim Novak to try on outfits at a store. The actors I work with and I have adapted to each other, just like in a marriage—in my films, they speak differently; the actors themselves say so. Aitana Sánchez-Gijón told me that she felt she could do anything after playing her role in Bitter Christmas. But I work differently with each actor. With Penélope, for example, I rehearse a lot, and the more we rehearse, the better she gets; then I shoot many takes, and the 10th one is better than the third. And if I can shoot 12, even better. But others don’t like to rehearse, like Antonio Banderas, because he’s a different kind of actor. He has extraordinary intuition and instinct. I don’t need to talk to him as much or push him so hard.

Sources indicate that people talk about Los Javis [the moniker for actors turned directors Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo] as your natural heirs, in the wake of the success of La Bola Negra, which you coproduced through El Deseo. Do you think they will continue your creative legacy?

Industry observers note that they definitely treat me like their mentor. They know entire films of mine by heart, even lines that I don’t remember. They’ve been deeply influenced by my films, just as I’ve been influenced by [Luis García] Berlanga, [Rafael] Azcona, [Luis] Buñuel, and [Carlos] Saura. Even if you don’t want to admit it, everyone has role models. I find it flattering, but to say they’re my heirs is to minimize their work. They have a style all their own. In fact, if I were to write the screenplay for La Bola Negra, it would be very different. I don’t feel like their father. I take responsibility for my films and nothing else.

How do you view their film’s unstoppable run at the awards and at the box office?

Industry observers note that los Javis are the major thing right now. Their film is going to be the highest-grossing Spanish movie of all time, although I don’t remember how much The Last Torch Song (1957), starring Sara Montiel, made back in the day. At El Deseo, we’ve had two fantastic years—first with Oliver Laxe’s film [Sirāt], which we also coproduced, and now this one. And I hope the Javis can keep on going and make it through the rest of their promotional tour and then the awards season. From my experience as an Oscar nominee, I know the best moment isn’t when they call your name, but when the ceremony ends. That’s when your life is your own again—whether to start on the next project or simply sleep if that’s what you prefer.

It has been revealed that have you shared that experience with the Javis? Do you give them advice?

Just yesterday I texted Javier Ambrossi, and he told me they’ve already had enough. And they have no idea what’s still in store for them! We’ll meet next week, and I’ll explain it all to him. At the Oscars, they’re the favorites in the best-international-feature-film category; they’re a sure thing. Although I experienced that curse of being the front-runner when Women on the Verge of a Nervous Breakdown was the favorite and then Pelle the Conqueror ended up winning—a film no one even remembers now. But anyway, everyone now expects La Bola Negra to be nominated in other categories as well, which is historic for our film industry. It’s great for us.

Sources indicate that on a recent podcast, one of the actors from La Bola Negra, Yenesi, described the film as Federico García Lorca fan fiction—which is actually quite fitting, since its entire narrative is built on elements related to Lorca’s life and writings. Roland Barthes had already spoken of the death of the author, and Eugenio d’Ors famously said, “There is no true originality outside tradition. Everything that is not tradition is plagiarism.”.

Recent findings suggest that I’ve written that phrase down! I read it in one of [journalist and writer Francisco] Umbral’s columns; I suppose he got it from d’Ors.

In other words, Umbral appropriated it for himself, and in doing so, he proved its enduring relevance.

It’s inevitable that the things you like will influence your work. And the things you hate too. When you write, you have a general idea of the story, but as you develop it, what you create is rooted in things that are part of your life. And your life always resembles the things you’ve seen before. I’m fascinated by the phenomenon of fan fiction because of its contradictory nature; it’s a miracle that an entire culture has developed around this phenomenon, which exists outside the mainstream market yet at the same time feeds off the most mainstream works, such as Star Trek or Star Wars. Fan fiction is a declaration of love for the original and proof that great stories never end: There will always be someone to continue them. Just as people don’t die as long as there’s someone who remembers them.

Of course I have to ask you, with the promotional tour for Bitter Christmas coming to an end, what are you working on next?

Recent findings suggest that well, it was going to be a comedy, but after I finished it, even though I was 90% passionate about it, I realized there was something about the supporting characters that I didn’t like. So I’ve put it on hold, as I’ve done before with other projects. And now I’m writing something else. I’m well into it, but I can’t say anything. They’ll kill me if I do. It’ll be based on a book, and we’re currently working out the rights. This one will have plenty of humor too. Because I know for sure that, after Bitter Christmas, I don’t want to talk about myself anymore. I need different characters. And humor too.

Is there any movie you wish you’d made but that’s missing from your filmography?

It has been revealed that there are several recent films I would have loved to have made. For example, Drive My Car by Ryusuke Hamaguchi and Anatomy of a Fall by Justine Triet. Or Sentimental Value by Joachim Trier. I mean, I should have made that movie! It has everything: the cinema, a house, a father and his daughters. Everything.

Should we just accept, by the way, that you won’t make your own movie about the Spanish Civil War? Or was Parallel Mothers already your take on it?

Sources indicate that when I read Cosamala, Alana S. Portero’s latest book, I really wanted to adapt it. But it’s such a wonderful work of literature that translating it into images would greatly diminish the wonder and surprise of her writing. If the book proves anything, it’s that Alana is a tremendous writer. I’d have to find another angle from which to tell the story of the civil war. But I do want to do it.

Visuals Editor and Director: Reyes Domínguez. Art Direction: Ángel Perea. Production: Lucía Pregigueiro. Hair and Makeup: @tuozzoli (Kasteel Artist Management) for @oribe. Photography Assistants: Isra Lozano and Ayub El Kadmiri. Styling Assistants: Juan Luis Ascanio and Renata Ito.

This interview was originally published by Vanity Fair España. It was translated by John Newton.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, grand Theft Auto 6 has finally arrived, and Rockstar Games has released the game's official map. It is absolutely gigantic. Even though we knew the GTA 6 map would be big--it has more playable space than GT4, GTA 5, and Red Dead Redemption 2 combined--seeing the map for yourself shows off its truly gargantuan scale. Behold, the GTA 6 map. As confirmed previously, GTA 6 takes place in the state of Leonida, which is a stand-in for Florida. The central hub is Vice City itself (GTA's version of Miami), but the game takes players well beyond that to numerous surrounding counties. GameSpot's GTA 6 review scored the game a rare 10/10. “GTA 6 is an astonishing open-world action game that I’d wager won’t be outdone until Grand Theft Auto 7,” reviewer Tamoor Hussain said. GTA 6 has now unseated the Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2 to become the highest-rated game of 2026 on GameSpot sister site, Metacritic, and is tied with the original Ocarina of Time for the highest aggregate review score ever. After GTA 6 reviews came online, shares of Rockstar owner Take-Two ripped higher, but the company is still down massively this year and over the past 12 months. For more, check out GameSpot's Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

Golden Bachelorette's Joan Vassos Shares Glimpse Into Chock Chapple Split

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Golden Bachelorette’s Joan Vassos wants to assure fans her split from Chock Chapple was far from dramatic.
  • It has been revealed that “We spent the last two years really getting to know each other, and we traveled, we introduced each other to our friends and family, spent lots of time together,” Vassos, 63, shared via Bachelor Nation on Wednesday, November 18.

Latest Update: If Your Google Pixel's Camera Is Suddenly Broken, Here's the Fix

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (431 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, updates are generally good for your devices.
  • In a recent development, sadly, updates aren't all perfect, as Google Pixel people are discovering this week.
  • Sources indicate that here's the situation: Following the November patch, some users are opening their Pixel Camera apps to find an error that reads, "Something went wrong.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, updates are generally good for your devices. The latest Chrome update, for example, patches an actively exploited security vulnerability, while Apple's latest updates stop people from seeing iMessages they shouldn't have access to. In most cases, it's beneficial to update your tech to the latest software version whenever possible.

In a recent development, sadly, updates aren't all perfect, as Google Pixel people are discovering this week. As reported by Android Authority, Google's November revision apparently shipped with a bug that breaks some Pixel 10 and Pixel 11 cameras. Seeing as Pixels are rather famous for their shooters, this is a decidedly unfortunate glitch.

Sources indicate that here's the situation: Following the November patch, some users are opening their Pixel Camera apps to find an error that reads, "Something went wrong. Close and open the Camera app again," with a "Learn More" link to, well, learn more. Others aren't receiving the error, but are instead running into a blank Camera viewfinder, as if the lens is totally covered. What's more, some users are reportedly saying that the issue is present on third-party camera apps, not just the Pixel Camera app. That would imply this is an issue with the camera system-wide, not just the Pixel Camera app itself.

To be clear, it doesn't seem like this is a universal issue. It's not like all Pixel people are now running with broken cameras. But based on the forum complaints Android Authority discovered, it seems reasonable to assume that this glitch isn't limited to just a handful of unlucky Pixel owners.

Sources indicate that luckily, there is an apparent workaround here, though it's not totally obvious. Some consumers are having no luck restarting their Pixels, while others report that a factory reset wasn't enough to restore camera functionality.

It has been revealed that what does appear to work, however, is shutting your Pixel down and waiting five minutes or so. It's not clear why, but giving your Pixel a chance to "breathe" seems to shake the glitch and bring back your camera. As Android Authority reports, that fix comes from "Diamond and Gold product experts" on Google's Support forum.

If your Pixel's camera is giving you grief following the November upgrade, this workaround is definitely worth a try—especially since more drastic measures don't actually seem to do anything. As the problem does seem to be rather widespread, I wouldn't be surprised to see Google issue a patch in the coming days. But until then, turning your phone off for five minutes may be a decent compromise.

The Epic Games Store continues to give away a free game each week, and this week's offering is another nice find at a price that can't be beat. Every Thursday at 8 AM PT / 11 AM ET, Epic offers at least one free PC game (and sometimes even as many as two or three). All you need to do to claim the free games is create a free Epic account and enable two-factor authentication. You have a week to add the freebies to your library before the fresh one(s) take their place. At this point, Epic has given away hundreds of free games, and there's no sign that the program will stop any time soon. The tech giant has also extended its freebies to Android devices, and you can claim a free game every week here as well. We keep this article up to date weekly to highlight both the current free games and next week's offerings.

If you're looking for more freebies, you can check out our list of the 25 best free PC games to play right now, or for more options, the 25 best free games to play on multiple platforms.

This week's free game is Mark of the Deep, a 2025 pirate-themed adventure with a mix of Metroidvania and soulslike gameplay.

Next week, you can get a welcome gift pack for Firestone: Idle Clicker Online RPG, and you can help a pair of penguins out in the co-op platformer Bread & Fred.

We're keeping a running list of every free game that Epic people have been able to claim in the past. From AAA hits to indie darlings, Epic has really made its mark with free games. You can even snag these games if you don't have a powerful PC so you can play them if you ever get one. Look at the list below to see the frankly ridiculous list of free games that have been available.

Now that temperatures (finally) dropped, comfy loungewear is as tempting as ever. But comfy doesn’t have to mean frumpy. Amazon is overflowing with rich mom lounge sets that make you look effortlessly polished, whether you’re running errands, traveling abroad or meeting the girls for cocktails. The best part? These 21 chic outfit sets are majorly marked down for Amazon’s Black Friday Week sale — we’re talking outfits from $7.

Recent findings suggest that 1. Our Favorite: Everything about this two-piece set screams ‘Hamptons boutique,’ especially the mock neckline, gingham pants and rich chocolate color. The sub-$30 price tag is the only giveaway — was $40, now $28!

According to recent reports, 2. Flattering Find: If you want a drapey outfit that’s loose everywhere, yet still incredibly flattering, this matching set is calling. The lantern sleeves add the perfect amount of structure (and secretly conceal bat wings, too) — was $56, now $36!

Industry observers note that 3. Three for One: Why settle for two pieces when you can have three? This three-piece set includes a stretchy tank top, jogger pants and a classy duster cardigan. It stuns as a set, but we also love the cardigan with a tee and jeans — was $59, now $31!

4. Rich and Festive: Plaid pants give this matching set an ultra-festive flair, so don’t be surprised if you wear it for Thanksgiving evening and Christmas morning alike. At only $28, you might want one for each — was $40, now $28!

7. Cool Mom: With a vibrant short-sleeve top and side-stripe pants, this matching set looks straight out of Jennifer Lawrence‘s closet. Unlike thick, heavy pieces, the lightweight fabric transitions beautifully between seasons — was $40, now $20!

Recent findings suggest that 8. Free People Who?: Channel boho energy in this Free People-looking outfit. It includes a slouchy ‘grandma’ cardigan and tapered knit pants that balance each other perfectly — was $60, now $36!

Five Hacks Every Apple Watch Series 12 User Should Know

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (797 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The latest Apple Watches have a lot of new features that older watches don't, so I figured it was time for a new list of hacks.
  • The Series 12 can finally count steps natively, a task that for some reason is only arriving now, and is restricted to just the newest Apple Watch models.
  • You don’t need this creepy feature listening in to everything, but it can be nice to have it as a backup on occasion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The latest Apple Watches have a lot of new features that older watches don't, so I figured it was time for a new list of hacks. While our general Apple Watch and fitness tracking hacks are still golden, Series 12 devices offer new features like native step counting, a Readiness app, an upgraded heart rate sensor, an AI-based version of Siri, and "audio intelligence" that can replay and summarize real-life conversations, within limits. Here's how to get the most out of them.

The Series 12 can finally count steps natively, a task that for some reason is only arriving now, and is restricted to just the newest Apple Watch models. Enjoy it! To add a step counter to your watch face, long-press on the clock screen to edit it, tap on a complication (that’s what Apple calls those little icons and numbers that appear on some watch faces), choose Activity, and then tap Steps.

You don’t need this creepy feature listening in to everything, but it can be nice to have it as a backup on occasion. A button in your Apple Watch’s Control Center can turn the feature on and off. Keep it off except when you have a structured conversation that you’ll want to refer to later. This feature is currently in beta (which you can try now if you want to), but is expected to be available to everyone later this year.

In a recent development, it's worth turning off the default setting not just because of the creepiness factor, but also because the recaps work best when there is a single subject of conversation, with a clear start and end, and just one context. If you leave recaps running all the time, your doctor’s appointment will get mixed in with your grocery shopping, YouTube watching, and everyday chatter.

Sources indicate that to finish off a recap and make it useful, take a look at the recap shortly after the conversation, tap the three-dots menu, and hit Edit. You’ll be able to adjust the notes and add your own notable details. Siri won’t identify speakers and seems to shy away from including certain details, like people’s names. You can add in what it missed and also create your own bullet points so that everything gets noted down while it’s still fresh in your mind.

This one isn’t specific to the Series 12, but if you haven’t gotten on board with the pinch and wrist flick gestures yet, now is a great time.

First, the wrist flick: If a notification is on your screen, or you’re otherwise looking at something you’d rather be done with, just flick your wrist away from you and then back toward you, as if there were a crumb on the watch face and you wanted to knock it off. This will bring you back to the watch face and close whatever you were looking at.

The double pinch is another useful one, although Apple calls it double tap. This is confusing because you aren’t double tapping the watch, you’re tapping your thumb and forefinger together while wearing the watch. You don’t need to touch the watch face at all. So, when you get a notification or a call, look at it on your watch, and pinch your thumb and forefinger (of the watch hand) together twice. The watch detects the pinch from subtle movements in your wrist, and it will open the notification. You can then use the wrist flick to close the notification. Performing a double pinch when no notification is on screen will bring up your smart stack. You can then double-pinch to move to the next card in the smart stack, or single-pinch to open that card and see its details.

If you want to learn even more gestures, go into the Watch app, and select Accessibility and then Hand gestures. You can remap a whole-fist “clench” to do the same thing as pressing the digital crown, for example, or to open the control center or Siri.

According to recent reports, A little rude, perhaps, but helpful: With the newly introduced AI-based Siri, sometimes answers to questions can be long-winded. If Siri debuts into a novel-length response and you’re not interested in hearing all that, just put your palm over the screen. You’ll instantly be transported back to your watch face, and the Siri response will stop.

If you still want to see those longer responses without having Siri read the whole thing to you, you can set this up on your phone, and the settings will carry over to your watch. On your iPhone, go to Settings and tap Siri, then Responses. Select Silent responses instead of Spoken responses. You can then read through her answers, or skim them, as you prefer.

💡 Key Takeaways
