Tech Report: WoW: Forever Wants To Get Rid Of The Idea Of “BiS” Gear

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1462 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • World of Warcraft: Forever is approaching itemization and "best-in-slot" (BiS) gear differently, with developer Blizzard instead wanting players to have more boss- or biome-specific choices.
  • World of Warcraft: Forever is approaching itemization and "best-in-slot" (BiS) gear differently, with developer Blizzard instead wanting players to have more boss- or biome-specific choices.
  • In the latest episode of the WoW: Forever Podcast, Blizzard dove deep on the MMORPG's itemization changes, how it approached designing Forever's newly introduced items, class changes, and more.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

World of Warcraft: Forever is approaching itemization and "best-in-slot" (BiS) gear differently, with developer Blizzard instead wanting players to have more boss- or biome-specific choices. In the latest episode of the WoW: Forever Podcast, Blizzard dove deep on the MMORPG's itemization changes, how it approached designing Forever's new items, class changes, and more. On the subject of raid gear and chase items, Forever senior game designer Aidan Moon said something that could be seen as controversial in certain circles of the game's community. "I essentially want to get rid of BiS," Moon said. "I think that BiS is not a good thing for a video game that's supposed to be about [the] role-playing aspects of it." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=67dDe3QgJtM BiS is WoW shorthand for essentially the best item that could possibly be in a given gear slot for a specific class. Look up any WoW guide for WoW Classic or modern WoW, and you'll find class BiS gear lists telling players exactly what they should be wearing in order for their character to be as powerful as possible. Endgame in many ways revolves around acquiring your BiS gear, first your "pre-raid" BiS from gear available in max-level dungeons, and then BiS gear, like tier sets, from raids. It's for that exact reason Forever introduced new items that grant additional stats or effects against certain enemy types or even in certain locations. Moon gave an example of specific items that deal more damage against Murloc enemies, and that players might want to have more gear tailored to fighting against a Murloc boss in a raid encounter. Forever's raids will feature multiple distinct biomes within them, Moon revealed, giving players more factors to consider when choosing what gear to use for specific parts of each raid. One wing of a raid may be snowy, while another may be cavernous, changing what gear could be more optimal for those encounters. "I think your BiS should be different [for] every single boss if you're actually making a theoretical BiS list," Moon said. "It should be based on the creature and the biome and a mixture of those two. You might have an item that's really good against snowy, and then another item in that same slot that's really good against Murlocs. Then there's a Murloc boss in a snowy area and you're just like 'Which one do I wear?' And then eventually you get to a point where you're swapping those things out or it's too much cognitive load and you don't want to do that. It's for those players that really want to optimize."  Trying to get rid of BiS lists is a substantial change for WoW, which has revolved around the idea for over two decades. Players can already encounter some of the itemization ideas Moon discussed while leveling to 60, with low-level gear from dungeons and quests dealing more damage against specified enemy types or even granting additional movement speed in specific zones. "I don't want you to have to ever think about BiS, I just want you to think about the fight right in front of you and how you're going to fight it," Moon said. Of course, having more biome- or enemy-type-specific items means hoarding more pieces of gear as opposed to selling old ones when an upgrade comes around. That will no doubt quickly fill up the inventories and banks of players looking to min-max for every possible scenario. Classic WoW is already notorious for having limited bag space, and players running around with multiple sets of hyper-specific gear will only make that pain point worse. Blizzard sounds like it's aware of that problem. Principal game designer Kris Zierhut said bigger bags are on that way, but that it's not needed right now immediately post-launch. However, Blizzard knows players will eventually need more bag space as well as better ways to organize and search for owned items to make putting together encounter-specific sets of gear easier. It's a massive change, but the strategy Blizzard is employing seems to be working. Forever's launch broke WoW concurrent and weekly player records, and more than 15 million characters have been created in the MMO so far. Blizzard recently lifted the veil on how Forever's new PvP system will work, revealing how classic WoW's infamous rank grind will now be a thing of the past.

#51225. 10 Years Ago Today: The Harry Potter Universe Expanded With A Star-Studded Spin-Off

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (827 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Slashfilm ↗ Open Full Page

10 Years Ago Today: The Harry Potter Universe Expanded With A Star-Studded Spin-Off

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (827 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Slashfilm

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
  • "Harry Potter" is perhaps the defining franchise of the 2000s, but all good things must come to an end.
  • Set decades before Harry Potter was even born, 2016's "Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them," which opened 10 years ago today, brought the action to America and focused on entirely latest characters within the Wizarding World.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

"Harry Potter" is perhaps the defining franchise of the 2000s, but all good things must come to an end. That end originally came in 2011 with "Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows – Part 2" which had the biggest opening ever up to that point in cinema history. But creator J.K. Rowling and Warner Bros. weren't content to let the Wizarding World end there. Ten years ago, they expanded the universe with a star-studded spin-off.

Set decades before Harry Potter was even born, 2016's "Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them," which opened 10 years ago today, brought the action to America and focused on entirely latest characters within the Wizarding World. Specifically Newt Scamander, played by Oscar-winner Eddie Redmayne. Redmayne had an unexpected inspiration for his performance, namely film icon Buster Keaton. The movie itself was loosely based on an in-universe textbook mentioned in the main series, with Rowling eventually releasing a version of the book, though it didn't contain a narrative.

The resulting prequel/spin-off takes place in 1926 centered on magizoologist Newt Scamander as he arrives in New York during a worldwide tour to research and rescue magical creatures. A mysterious magical being begins causing chaos in NYC, which threatens to expose the wizarding world to the muggles of Earth.

In a recent development, redmayne was far from the only big star to secure a role in the spin-off. The stacked cast also includes but is not limited to Katherine Waterston, Dan Fogler, Alison Sudol, Samantha Morton, Ezra Miller, and Colin Farrell. "Fantastic Beats" also cast Johnny Depp as Grindelwald in a surprise appearance. Arguably the most notable casting decision the movie made, with the benefit of hindsight.

J.K. Rowling wrote the script for "Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them" personally, which wasn't the case with the other "Harry Potter" movies. David Yates, who helmed the final four "Harry Potter" movies, was recruited to tackle the spin-off as well, providing a sturdy hand.

In a recent development, the majority of the core cast were on the upswing. This movie was expected to be a big break for all of them. In many ways, it was. "Fantastic Beasts" was dubbed a worthy extension of the Wizarding World in many reviews, with audiences tending to agree. Even if it wasn't effusive praise, it was good enough.

The movie was released in November 2016 and did quite well for itself, pulling in $816 million at the global box office. That was more than enough to convince Warner Bros. to double down, with four "Fantastic Beasts" sequels revealed before the first one even hit theaters. Everyone involved fully expected this to be the long-term future for the "Harry Potter" franchise. What's perhaps most surprising about that, especially in light of the first movie's success, is the fact that the words Harry Potter don't appear anywhere in the title. All the same, audiences found it.

The train had left the station and everyone involved had every reason to believe, on paper, that people would show up for the sequels en masse. After all, the first installment scored well enough with critics and was the eighth-biggest movie of 2016 overall. Unfortunately, the future had different looks.

Warner Bros. and director David Yates wasted no time, with the second "Fantastic Beasts" installment dated for November 2018. Much of the cast returned, with new additions entering the fold. But in no small part due to forces beyond the studio's control, "The Crimes of Grindelwald" doomed "Fantastic Beasts.".

Recent findings suggest that the sequel pulled in more than $650 million at the box office, but made a lot less domestically and had to rely on international audiences to bail it out. Then there's the Depp of it all. Controversy started swirling around the actor due to his public feud with his ex-wife Amber Heard, involving accusations of domestic abuse. Depp later dropped out of the "Fantastic Beasts" franchise following a court case verdict. Mads Mikkelsen took over as Grindelwald in "The Secrets of Dumbledore," but the writing was on the wall.

The third installment made hardly more than $400 million globally, failing to break even theatrically. "The Secrets of Dumbledore" proved that the magic was gone, despite the appeal of Jude Law as a younger Albus Dumbledore in a lead role. The cast continued to be star-studded all along the way but, at a certain point, appealing casts only go so far. Especially in the 2020s when audiences are more content than ever to stay at home and stream something from the couch.

According to recent reports, controversy and middling results with diminishing returns eventually derailed "Fantastic Beasts." Ten years ago though, the spin-off arrived with a great deal of promise and a lot of potential. That potential just never proved out.

You can grab "Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them" on 4K, Blu-ray, or DVD from Amazon.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that young men in relationships around the world have spent the last few weeks warning their significant others about Nov.
  • Recent findings suggest that these men, who were planning on abandoning their girlfriends for an undetermined amount of time, logged in to Rockstar's game on Thursday night to find another expectant woman waiting on the other side.
  • “What is this cuck simulator?” said one popular streamer whose clips of discomfort with Jason and Lucia's relationship have gone viral online.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that young men in relationships around the world have spent the last few weeks warning their significant others about Nov. 19. On that day, and for their forseeable future, the men in their lives would be MIA, they noted. They wouldn't answer texts. They weren't going to hang out. Many women were told to accept that men would put little to no effort into their relationships for a while as they focused entirely on Grand Theft Auto 6.

Recent findings suggest that these men, who were planning on abandoning their girlfriends for an undetermined amount of time, logged in to Rockstar's game on Thursday night to find another expectant woman waiting on the other side. Her name was Lucia, and she couldn't fully be brushed off — not if the player wanted to have a positive experience with the game's main story, anyway.

“What is this cuck simulator?” said one popular streamer whose clips of discomfort with Jason and Lucia's relationship have gone viral online. Although actively recoiling is an extreme reaction to GTA 6, the men doing so are emblematic of a wider trend of confusion and disgust with the game's relationship-driven experience.

"This game is woke slop," another male player complained after discovering a mission that tasked them with buying flowers for Lucia. "It's obvious it was made by women.".

"I'm just going to kill myself, what the fuck," a player wrote in a viral video that called GTA 6 a "latina dating simulator." The footage highlights the couple moving furniture and watching TV together.

Industry observers note that rockstar Games has made no secret that the relationship between Jason and Lucia was a central element of their upcoming game. The studio has likened the pair to a modern Bonnie and Clyde. Much of the marketing has focused on the mechanics Rockstar built to help players develop that relationship, like having small check-ins or going on dates.

For a good while, the men on the other side of those advertisements were fully on board. Lucia is hot, so what's not to like? On popular online communities like Reddit, most of the top posts about the game leading up to release were men sharing AI-generated images of Lucia naked, or in revealing clothing. The men were so into Lucia as an idea that when an apparent hacker proposed leaking nude gameplay of Lucia, the rogue was able to raise millions of real-world dollars.

According to recent reports, men couldn't get enough of Lucia ... until they actually got to experience her. To be clear, GTA 6 doesn't position Lucia as a nagging woman with annoying demands. Lucia is in prison at the start of the game, and players take control right before she is released. Jason's first story missions focus on classic GTA action, like driving, drugs, and making money. The game ambiently tells fans that they can do specific things to help prepare for Lucia's arrival, like painting the walls or patching her home's leaky roof. These activities are so subtle that some players probably miss them. Certainly, they could be disregarded altogether.

GTA 6's release is an event for women and men alike, but the game’s cultural identity is an unusually gendered one. Mainstream publications covering the game often do so by parsing it through the lens of heterosexual relationships. Here, people indulged in gendered thought experiments like “Is dating Lucia considered cheating for men?” One of the most pervasive GTA 6 memes frameworks dealt with men's anxieties about juggling GTA 6's release with the demands of their existing relationships.

In a recent development, GTA 6 is a video game, though, and gamers have a compulsion to do everything they can. Games position players to be the good guys, but the fantasy is easier to uphold when it's an abstract tale of good versus evil. When playing a game ostensibly means upkeep like showering your crusty character because your girlfriend thinks you reek, any semblance of a traditional power fantasy is shattered.

"10 hrs in and the game is just a chore simulator," one fan complained in a thread with dozens of replies debating whether Rockstar's latest could truly be considered a GTA game. In it, fans recognize GTA 6 still technically allows them to do most of the signature activities the franchise is known for. The big difference is that this time, Rockstar places empathy at the forefront. This change of direction is present in Jason and Lucia's relationship, but it's also evident throughout the rest of the game. You can absolutely start a rampage on a crowded beach — you just have to stomach killing some of the most realistic humans ever depicted in a video game.

Recent findings suggest that similarly, players can decide against nurturing their relationship with Lucia. The central story still revolves around the duo, and the two are fundamentally linked in a way I won't spoil. There's a version of GTA 6 that doesn't impose nonstop chores like buying groceries. Surprisingly, the game even allows you to forego picking Lucia up from prison. That playthrough comes with in-game arguments with Lucia that can escalate to a point where the two won't talk with one another much anymore.

Playing the story in GTA has always been optional, though. Historically, many fans haven't bothered with the narrative and approach the series as a free-roaming sandbox. That ethos is largely still tenable in GTA 6. The real question is whether players, particularly men, can stand being confronted with the disappointment of their actions.It may not be a lost cause. The same streamer who has accrued millions of views while recoiling from the screen, unable to watch Jason and Lucia's relationship play out, has readily called Jason a "simp" and GTA 6 a "female fantasy.".

"I'm enjoying the game," he stated in the same breath.

Latest Update: Avengers: Doomsday's PG-13 Rating Explained

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (556 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Slashfilm

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, we are a month away from potentially the biggest box office weekend of 2026, with Dunesday set to blow Barbenheimer out of the water as both "Dune: Part Three" and "Avengers: Doomsday" make their way into theaters.
  • In a recent development, to be sure, between Robert Downey Jr.
  • According to recent reports, hence, it's no surprise to learn that the new "Avengers" movie is now officially rated PG-13, just like almost every other previous film entry in the MCU since 2008 (save for "Deadpool & Wolverine").
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, we are a month away from potentially the biggest box office weekend of 2026, with Dunesday set to blow Barbenheimer out of the water as both "Dune: Part Three" and "Avengers: Doomsday" make their way into theaters. These movies are aimed at similar audiences, yet they're vastly different when it comes to their tones and approaches to adapting popular characters for the big screen. Indeed, where Denis Villeneuve's cinematic takes on the "Dune" books have so far been somber and introspective, the road to "Doomsday" has been paved almost entirely with nostalgia.

In a recent development, to be sure, between Robert Downey Jr. returning to the Marvel Cinematic Universe (this time to play Doctor Doom), the latest Avengers roster featuring multiple beloved characters from the MCU's past, and several actors reprising their roles from 20th Century Fox's "X-Men" films, "Doomsday" has had no problem catching the attention and interest of virtually every kind of moviegoer out there. After all, where "Dune: Part Three" can afford to target older audiences given the mature themes of its source material, "Doomsday" is aimed at everyone with a pulse and a heartbeat.

According to recent reports, hence, it's no surprise to learn that the new "Avengers" movie is now officially rated PG-13, just like almost every other previous film entry in the MCU since 2008 (save for "Deadpool & Wolverine"). Per FilmRatings.com, the film earned this rating from the Motion Picture Association (MPA) based on its "violence/action, bloody images, and language.".

Sources indicate that just in case it needs to be noted, "Avengers: Doomsday" was never going to be rated anything other than PG-13. The MCU's movies, in general, tend to feature too much intense action for any of them to garner a mere PG rating, yet they also tend to avoid going overboard into full-blown adult territory. At the same time, the explanation for its rating suggests "Doomsday" will make good on its promise of being one of the darker installments in the franchise.

In a recent development, keeping that in mind, Marvel Studios and Disney were never going to allow a movie as costly as this one to get slapped with an R rating either, lest it severely limit the number of people who can pay to see it in a theater. And yes, "Deadpool & Wolverine" managed to become a massive success with an R-rating, but that was a different situation. Since the first two "Deadpool" films had been R-rated, it might've actually hurt the movie financially if it had tried to take the larger "Deadpool" property in a more family-friendly direction.

It has been revealed that that's not to suggest that "Doomsday" won't be sufficiently dark or violent, though. Just too long ago, in fact, Sam Raimi pushed the PG-13 rating as far as humanly possible with 2022's "Doctor Strange In the Multiverse of Madness," the most gruesome Marvel movie yet. As you may recall, that film was filled with incredibly brutal death scenes, legitimate jump scares, and upsetting imagery that's not suitable for younger audiences. On the other hand, we can probably safely assume "Doomsday" won't push the envelope that far, given everything that's riding on it.

You can see what "Avengers: Doomsday" has to offer for yourself when it opens in theaters on December 18, 2026.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • As we march ever closer to "Avengers: Doomsday," it's easy to forget this movie was supposed to look very different.
  • Sources indicate that kang the Conqueror (Jonathan Majors), a time traveler who hails from the 31st century, appeared as the main villain of "Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania." A post-credits scene debuted the "Council of Kangs," or all of Kang's variants from a multiverse full of different timelines.
  • Industry observers note that yeah, not exactly the launching pad you want for your next Thanos.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As we march ever closer to "Avengers: Doomsday," it's easy to forget this movie was supposed to look very different. The original lead-in to "Avengers: Secret Wars" was supposed to be "Avengers: The Kang Dynasty," as directed by Destin Daniel Cretton (who had already helmed "Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings" for Marvel and would go on to direct "Spider-Man: Brand New Day").

Sources indicate that kang the Conqueror (Jonathan Majors), a time traveler who hails from the 31st century, appeared as the main villain of "Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania." A post-credits scene debuted the "Council of Kangs," or all of Kang's variants from a multiverse full of different timelines. But "Quantumania" earned unenthusiastic reviews upon its release in February 2023, and worse, Majors was arrested for assault the following month. (He was found guilty, and then fired by Marvel/Disney, in December 2023.).

Industry observers note that yeah, not exactly the launching pad you want for your next Thanos. Cue a pivot, and the announcement at San Diego Comic-Con 2024 that "Kang Dynasty" had been reworked into "Avengers: Doomsday," featuring Robert Downey Jr. returning to Marvel but as Doctor Doom, not Iron Man, as well as the return of "Infinity War" and "Endgame" directors Joe and Anthony Russo.

Recent findings suggest that now, this all seems like a "break glass in case of emergency" situation. But Marvel Studios President Kevin Feige, sitting down with Empire Magazine, now claims that even before "The Kang Dynasty" became "Doomsday," Kang was planned to be a red herring for Doom:.

Recent findings suggest that "People think there was a cause-and-effect with Jonathan's issues, and that certainly accelerated some things. But the Doom of it all was well underway before that. [...] It probably would still have been called 'The Kang Dynasty,' but it would have been a set-up for Doom, midway through that movie.".

Kevin Feige, noting the "very delicate" situation with Jonathan Majors, told Empire that "[Marvel] didn't want to rush into any rash decisions in terms of employment." He acknowledged the changes to "The Kang Dynasty" started after the bad reception and underperformance of "Quantumania," noting:.

Sources indicate that "'Quantumania' was not received the way we would have liked. There are many elements of that that we're proud of, the Kang performance being one of them. But we were changing [The Kang Dynasty] even at that point.".

Reading between the lines of Feige's claims, it would appear that once Majors was fired, the studio decided to push forward with Doom as the villain from the start instead of recasting Kang. But is this credible? I'll admit my first thought while reading this was, "Yeah, right!".

According to recent reports, in his Empire interview, Feige appears to say the plans to bring in Doom to supplant Kang happened after the release of "Quantumania" but before Majors' arrest. "Quantumania" was released on February 17, 2023, and Majors was arrested on March 25, 2023. That seems like a pretty slim window to rework "The Kang Dynasty.".

In November 2023, Variety reported that — at the annual Marvel Studios retreat held that past September — studio leadership was actively discussing how to move forward with Kang. ("Marvel is truly f***ed with the whole Kang angle," an insider was quoted as saying.) Apparently, the Marvel brain trust discussed replacing Kang with another villain, Doom specifically being named, as well as bringing back Avengers who died in "Endgame," like Robert Downey Jr. as Iron Man, to gin up excitement. As we now know, that's basically what Marvel did.

During a November 2023 appearance on the "Hot Mic" podcast, journalist Jeff Sneider claimed that Doom would appear in the then-upcoming "The Fantastic Four: First Steps" (which he did) as set up for him to show up in "Avengers: Secret Wars." However, Sneider stated in that same interview that, "It'd be inaccurate to say [Doom is] the villain.".

According to recent reports, but Doom is the villain of Marvel Comics overall. The only reason the Marvel Cinematic Universe waited so long to use him is because 20th Century Fox held the film rights to his character. Once the Disney and Fox merger was completed in 2019, and Doom became available to Marvel Studios, Doom had to be high on any list of characters being considered for inclusion.

The "Secret Wars" comics — both the 1984 original and the 2015 pseudo-remake — also feature Doom as the main villain. In both, he attains godlike power and rules over a domain called Battleworld. If you're adapting "Secret Wars," the thought of using Doom has to cross your mind.

Sources indicate that kevin Feige's claim that Doom would take over "midway" through "The Kang Dynasty" also aligns with supposed leaked plot summaries for "Doomsday," which assert that Doom initially presents himself as an ally before revealing his true intentions. If that's accurate, it appears the movie still has the broad structure of "The Kang Dynasty," just with no Kang.

On the other hand, "Secret Wars" (especially the 2015 one) is a culmination of Doom's character. Rushing right into him becoming a God Emperor of Battleworld, without him being the villain in a "Fantastic Four" movie first? Yeah, that sounds like something that was "accelerated," per Feige.

"Avengers: Doomsday" releases on December 18, 2026.

Latest Update: Google Killed Its Dark Web Report, but You Can Still Monitor Data Breaches

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (792 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Google’s Dark Web Report used to be the only consumer-focused platform that let people scan major data breaches, dark web marketplaces, and private forums to see if their personal information had ended up in the hands of hackers.
  • Industry observers note that google notes it sunsetted Dark Web Report because, although the information it provided was generally useful, the service failed to provide “helpful next steps” for owners whose data was found on the dark web.
  • Recent findings suggest that dark Web Report may not have been perfect, but it was the only early warning system of its kind that was available for personal use and let users run scans free of cost.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google’s Dark Web Report used to be the only consumer-focused platform that let people scan major data breaches, dark web marketplaces, and private forums to see if their personal information had ended up in the hands of hackers. But the organization discontinued the service at the start of 2026, with fresh scans stopping on Jan. 15 and all accounts deleted on Feb. 16.

Industry observers note that google notes it sunsetted Dark Web Report because, although the information it provided was generally useful, the service failed to provide “helpful next steps” for owners whose data was found on the dark web. Google promised a fresh service that would provide more actionable intel, but that service has yet to materialize, and there haven’t been any further announcements about it yet.

Recent findings suggest that dark Web Report may not have been perfect, but it was the only early warning system of its kind that was available for personal use and let users run scans free of cost. Now that it’s gone, however, there are plenty of other services that offer the same service at varying costs and levels of effectiveness. Let’s talk through the nature of the insight that Google's reports offered, how it collected that information in the first place, and what options exist in the market to replace it.

Google launched the Dark Web Report in March 2023 as a premium feature available to Google One people, but later extended it for free to anyone with a Google account and moved it to the "Results about you" dashboard.

According to recent reports, you'd set up a monitoring profile with your name, date of birth, physical address, phone number, emails, and Social Security Number if you lived in the U.S. After that, you could head to the dashboard anytime you wanted to run a free scan across dark web forums and marketplaces, publicly disclosed corporate data breaches, and other hidden online spaces to see if any of your personal information had shown up there. It was easy to use—but not a lot of people knew it existed in the first place.

According to recent reports, it’s unclear what prompted the internal decision at Google, but in the absence of concrete next steps, it is reasonable to think the reports could create panic for the uninitiated. There’s no way to remove your information from the dark web once it’s already in circulation there. Still, having an early warning so you could reset 2FA or self-lock your SSN isn’t without merit.

Industry observers note that but perhaps more importantly, most people with Google accounts didn’t know and hadn’t heard of the Dark Web Report’s existence. Google has likely taken it as a hint that users want more active remediation tools than simple alerts, which is why it’s now directing users to the Password Manager, Passkeys, and “Results about you” dashboard instead—though, again, the company hasn't followed through on a direct replacement for Dark Web Report, despite teasing such a feature.

Industry observers note that many of the top dark web scanners draw from the same well of information, scanning against major data breaches and dark web spaces. Several also offer breach notifications that send you email alerts when your details show up in a periodic scan. However, none of that is worth paying for because Have I Been Pwned or Mozilla Monitor cover those features quite well for free. Even the default password managers from Google and Apple come with some ability to monitor leaked credentials.

According to recent reports, there isn’t an easy way to scrub your information from the dark web once it ends up getting leaked. But you can take steps to protect sensitive information or financial data once you know there’s been a leak. If a password has been compromised, reset it immediately. Also, enable 2FA on the affected account for added security. Even better, switch to a passkey if that account supports it. If not, authenticator apps are a safer way to receive 2FA codes than standard SMS.

According to recent reports, if your Social Security number has been leaked, freeze your credit with Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion. You can do this by contacting each agency separately. Freezing your credit will prevent unauthorized credit withdrawals and protect your credit score from abuse by attackers. If one of your credit or debit card numbers has ended up in a breach, call your bank to freeze transactions on that card immediately.

According to recent reports, finally, get in the habit of using email aliases instead of sharing your actual email address with every platform and service provider. Addy.io and Proton’s SimpleLogin are both popular services that let you generate temporary email aliases that point to your inbox.

Magic: The Gathering Designer Reveals the Commander Trend He Wants to See More Of

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1001 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Polygon

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • While at MagicCon: Atlanta 2026, one of the trickier Magic: The Gathering Commander decks I faced was led by Maralen, Fae Ascendant, from Lorwyn Eclipsed.
  • According to recent reports, her strategy is fairly simple: Every time an elf or faerie you control enters the battlefield, you exile the top two cards of an opponent’s library and cast a spell of mana cost equal to or less than the number of elves and faeries you control for free.
  • “One thing I’ve pitched for years is this idea of team-up type legends,” Verhey noted during a roundtable interview at MagicCon attended by Polygon.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

While at MagicCon: Atlanta 2026, one of the trickier Magic: The Gathering Commander decks I faced was led by Maralen, Fae Ascendant, from Lorwyn Eclipsed. Presently the 40th most popular Commander, according to data from EDHREC, Maralen is a typal Commander, meaning that her abilities emphasize creature types. In this case, she’s all about two kinds of creatures rather than just one. Specifically, this is an elves and faeries Commander. Since her color identity has three colors — black, green, and blue — that gives every Maralen deck access to a wide variety of both creature types to leverage some massive payoffs.

According to recent reports, her strategy is fairly simple: Every time an elf or faerie you control enters the battlefield, you exile the top two cards of an opponent’s library and cast a spell of mana cost equal to or less than the number of elves and faeries you control for free. The results are always unpredictable, but how you get the engine going is easy. Play a ton of small faeries and elves and watch as you turn your opponents’ weapons against them. The impish flavor here feels perfect for the queen of the fae in Lorwyn, but the core design philosophy at play is something Magic’s principal designer Gavin Verhey wants to expand upon.

“One thing I’ve pitched for years is this idea of team-up type legends,” Verhey noted during a roundtable interview at MagicCon attended by Polygon. “Seeing the success of Maralen is making me want to do a lot more. There’s also my funky cat-zombie team-up in Mystery Booster Commander. That’s just fun to do, right? People love building around creature types. So why not two? These are the sort of things I want to do more of in the future.”.

Verhey served as lead designer of the newly released Mystery Booster Commander alongside co-lead Eric Engelhard. The “cat-zombie team-up” he mentions is Olag and Miau, Newly introduced Friends. An Abzan (white-black-green) legendary creature, Olag and Miau is the marriage of cats and zombies. Each time you cast a cat, you put a +1/+1 counter on a zombie you control. And every time you cast a zombie, you put a +1/+1 counter on one of your cats. Then at the end of your turn, all opponents also lose an amount of life equal to the number of tapped cats and zombies you control.

Industry observers note that as long as you keep attacking with those cats and zombies — or find some other way to tap them — you can easily whittle away at your opponents. The trade-off is that this leaves you potentially defenseless, so it’s a good thing that Abzan has plenty of lifegain options for you to balance things out. Had I come across Olag and Miau during my own Mystery Booster Commander pick-two draft at MagicCon, I definitely would have gone all-in on crafting that deck. Sadly, I did not.

In a recent development, another example of this kind of dual-typal strategy in your Command Zone that Verhey brought up is Rin and Seri, Inseparable. (Even more popular than Maralen at 38th on EDHREC, by the way.) Whenever you cast a dog, Rin and Seri create a 1/1 cat. Whenever you cast a cat, they create a 1/1 dog. It also has an activated ability that lets you deal damage equal to the number of dogs you have on the battlefield and heal yourself an amount based on the number of cats you control.

Though it’s technically illegal to play in all constructed formats, save for Mystery Booster Commander drafts and constructed events, there’s a ridiculous test card that riffs on this iconic duo — and it had me burst out laughing when I saw it. Rin and Seri, Inseperabler (yes, “Inseperable-r”) makes all of the cats you control gain the dog type and all dogs you control gain the cat type. And it gives them all haste. It’s tantalizing to think about a Commander deck that gets both versions of Rin and Seri on the battlefield. Every cat or dog you control then counts toward both halves of the original Rin and Seri’s activated ability, potentially doubling its potency.

It has been revealed that inseparabler isn’t exactly broken. It would be if its core abilities were blanket effects that made all cats dogs and vice versa rather than just the ones you control, because then every cat or dog you played would generate two 1/1 cat-dogs. My draft deck wound up being Selesnya (green-white), so Inseparabler was relegated to my sideboard. It’s not worth much money, but I am absolutely keeping it. Maybe I’ll go out of my way to buy the original Rin and Seri and build out the deck, perhaps with some way to tutor Inseperabler into play just to see how effectively it might snowball.

Another interesting example of this multi-typal design philosophy popped up in the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles set, in which plenty of cards care about mutants, ninjas, and, turtles. The five-color Heroes in a Half Shell legendary creature from the precon adds +1/+1 counters and draws a card when one or more of these creature types deal combat damage to a player. It’s another interesting experiment with typically disparate creature types, and it’s one that, in retrospect, I’m far more interested in building than I was previously.

Industry observers note that if cats can get along with both dogs and zombies, and faeries with elves, then what other fun typal combinations could emerge in Commander? If only the Lord of the Rings set had a Gruul (red-green) Gimli and Legolas Commander that united elves and dwarves, or perhaps Marvel: Darkhold Destiny could deliver the ideal gods and demons Commander? Universes Beyond might be uniquely suited to these kinds of quirky Commanders, but there’s space for it in all of Magic. And I’m very intrigued to see where Gavin Verhey and the rest of Magic’s design team might take it.

Want to Smell Bisexual? A Hit Podcast Has the Perfume for You

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1816 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You Must Remember This is a podcast dedicated, as its host Karina Longworth says in every intro, to exploring the secret and/or forgotten histories of Hollywood’s first century.
  • Longworth is a native Angeleno who has been writing about film for years.
  • The latest season of the podcast is called The Bisexuals, spotlighting the stories of actors and actresses whose love lives were often much more diverse than anything sanctioned by a studio.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You Must Remember This is a podcast dedicated, as its host Karina Longworth says in every intro, to exploring the secret and/or forgotten histories of Hollywood’s first century. Longworth, who is an LA–based writer and film preservationist, usually tells her stories in themed seasons. Those include Erotic 90’s, spanning the introduction of the NC-17 rating to Eyes Wide Shut; Dead Blondes (Marilyn Monroe, Jean Harlow, Veronica Lake); and a whole series exploring the web of connections Charles Manson had to Hollywood. It’s addictive, exhaustively researched, and narrated in a way that is both soothing and trancelike.

Longworth is a native Angeleno who has been writing about film for years. She was a film editor and critic at the LA Weekly for three years until 2012; wrote books on Al Pacino and Meryl Streep; and then started You Must Remember This is 2014. She’s also part of a film-loving couple: her husband of 8 years is the Knives Out writer and director Rian Johnson.

The latest season of the podcast is called The Bisexuals, spotlighting the stories of actors and actresses whose love lives were often much more diverse than anything sanctioned by a studio. One star that the season discusses is Libby Holman, a singer and socialite who married the tobacco heir Zachary Smith Reynolds in 1931. Not only did she have a fruitful sex life with Tallulah Bankhead and Montgomery Clift, but she was known for her signature scent called Jungle Gardenia.

In honor of that bombastic perfume that wafted off of her, Longworth, 46, collaborated with Joey Rosin, who formulated a fragrance, Bisexual. Vanity Fair spoke to Longworth about moviegoing in Los Angeles versus Upcoming York, what she smelled like as a teenager, being in grad school in your 40s, and her thoughts about Quentin Tarantino’s film programming.

The interview that follows has been condensed for length and clarity.

Vanity Fair: What was the first perfume you remember wearing?

Industry observers note that karina Longworth: Coco Mademoiselle was really a big deal for me when I was 18, 19. It was one of the first perfumes that I ever knew about. I started with The Body Shop’s Tea Rose oil. I didn’t really have any female adult influences because my mom died when I was 11, and so I had to sort of figure out that whole world.

Recent findings suggest that have you always wanted to make a perfume? Are you a perfume nerd?

According to recent reports, so I never had an ambition to make a perfume, but over the past 10 years, I’ve become really into perfume. I used to rent an office space in the same building as an independent perfumer, Jacqueline Ella Steele, whose brand was called Goest— which doesn’t exist anymore—but she made a perfume called Silent Films. She was the first person I contacted about trying to formulate this perfume. But she’s out of business. So that’s when I started asking around and I got led to Joey Rosin.

The idea came from your research?

I got the idea because, in reading and writing about Libby Holman, there are all these anecdotes of her walking into a room in a cloud of Jungle Gardenia, to the point where, people who were attracted to her were attracted to it, and people who didn’t like her found it so disgusting. I thought there was something really interesting about that, how the same scent could be either attractive or repellent, depending on how you felt about the person wearing it.

According to recent reports, what does a bisexual smell like? In this case jungles and gardenia.

Personalities, voices and clothes all depend on who’s doing it.

There’s this really incredible anecdote in Patricia Bosworth’s Montgomery Clift biography about how one of Montgomery Clift’s friends was at a party at Treetops, Libby Holman’s estate, and she was looking for the bathroom, and accidentally walked into her bedroom, and the bed was a tangle of white satin sheets, and there’s a giant bottle of barbiturates on the nightstand and everything just reeked of Jungle Gardenia. She was grossed out, but then she also got the impression this is Libby and Monty’s sex lair.

Were you trying to recreate the smell?

Sources indicate that we didn’t try to copy the exact old fragrance. Joey does his research, and he did research into what the original notes were. But we talked about not wanting it to be a slavish copy, and instead just trying to evoke for both of us what jungle would smell like with gardenia, and how that could evoke Libby’s story. And so we played around with adding different types of smoke to it.

Have you ever been in a jungle?

I’ve been to Tahiti. I’m trying to think if I’ve ever been to a jungle. We talked a lot about tropical plants and what the dirt would smell like, and the heat. It’s like hot weather almost has a smell. But then pairing that with this kind of old lady scent of gardenia. I went to visit his studio in Brooklyn a few times and he mailed some samples to me in Los Angeles. And by that point, it was like four iterations that were almost exactly the same. So it was just about what was giving me the best vibe.

You were living in LA for the process?

Industry observers note that I was living alone in Rochester, N.Y. in a depressing situation because of the weather and being very alone, having no social life.

Industry observers note that but you loved your grad school program, right? I forget the name but I know it’s long.

L. Jeffrey Selznick School of Film Preservation at the George Eastman Museum. I got so much out of the program, but it was grueling, physically, and mentally, and emotionally. It was really difficult to suddenly be living alone in a place where I felt like I had no one I could really talk to.

So you were in an entirely new, but temporary situation.

According to recent reports, I started relying on scented candles to improve my mood and to change my mood. If I got home feeling terrible, the fragrance was helpful. I also had nowhere to wear perfume. At first I thought I would just make a candle, and then as I started learning more about fragrance, I learned that candles have to go through a much more rigorous process. And it takes a lot longer. We were not going to be able to get it done in time to have a presale like we have during the podcast season. But in the future, I would like to do a signature scent for You Must Remember This and have it available as a perfume and a candle.

In a recent development, it would be classic, but in a different way. I’m very inspired by the signature scent that they have at the Chateau [Marmont].

Industry observers note that there has been a lot of talk about moviegoing being back. How has your tour been?

It has been great. In Savannah they sold 400 tickets to a very obscure, pre-code movie on a Friday night.

It has been revealed that people must ask you a lot of podcast questions. What are your tips?

I say I don’t know what form yours is going to take, but mine takes the form of writing an extremely detailed script, and then sitting by myself in a room and reading it into a microphone.

Sources indicate that I built a recording studio. I bought a little house in Laurel Canyon at the end of a private road, like at the end of a cul-de-sac, but you feel like you’re in the middle of the forest. I bought it from this woman who had lived there for 15 years and was kind of an all-purpose healer. She basically built a soundproof room with clay on the walls and crystals embedded into the clay, where she would do sound baths with them. When I saw this house, it was just perfect.

Which city has a better movie scene, New York or LA?

Latest York’s way better than LA, but LA is getting better.

Did someone buy the Vista? I loved that theater.

Recent findings suggest that [Quentin] Tarantino owns the Vista. Because it’s Tarantino, he won’t let them show anything digital. It has to be a film print, and so he’ll show a newly introduced movie if there’s a print, like The Odyssey played there, Sinners played there. But when there isn’t a new movie out that is on a print, he programs whatever he wants to see. He also does a lot of like Saturday morning matinees of classical Hollywood cinema that is just his taste, you know. Sometimes it’s my taste, sometimes it’s not. It’s a lot of Jerry Lewis. But one thing I will say for Tarantino is that when he discovers a filmmaker or genre or something from the past, he highlights. He’s been showing all these William Beaudine silent films, and I think that’s great because silent film has really fallen out of fashion in LA.

Sources indicate that I was leaving to interview you today and someone remarked, “Oh, I love that podcast,” and was talking about the Manson series. Is that your most popular?

It changes. Increasingly, people are asking about the Polly Platt series.

Do you know what the next series is going to be?

I have two ideas that would involve talking to people or family members of subjects who have passed away, but who could give me access to sort of the family lore. I am in contact with both of those families, but I need to kind of do the legwork, talking to them more and figure out which story makes the most sense. I also sketched out a very long season about the three stars of Rebel Without a Cause. That is something that people have been asking me to do for years. But the thing that stops me from doing it is that we still don’t know exactly what happened to Natalie Wood. But that’s kind of in my back pocket.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every new fantasy movie wants to be the next "Lord of the Rings," and every new fantasy TV series wants to be the next "Game of Thrones." But both mediums are littered with the corpses of projects that failed to capture the zeitgeist. That includes perfect little gems like "Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves" (whose box office underperformance remains a crushing shame) and "The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power" (which has proven it's not easy to be "Game of Thrones" for a "Lord of the Rings" audience, even with a billion dollar budget).

According to recent reports, recently, you may have noticed a upcoming fantasy franchise waiting in the wings. Well, "new" isn't the proper word, perhaps — millions of people are very familiar with it. But rather, new to the people who made "Lord of the Rings" and "Game of Thrones" a crossover success. I'm talking about Magic: The Gathering, the long-running fantasy card game that's been draining wallets and firing up imaginations since its debut in 1993, which is now poised to make the leap to the significant and small screens with two different projects.

The first of them is a Netflix animated series called "Planeswalker" from showrunner Terry Matalas, who's already a geek favorite thanks to his strong work on "Star Trek: Picard" season 3 and Marvel's "VisionQuest." The second is a live-action feature film starring Maya Hawke from Legendary Pictures and Matt Johnson, the eclectic filmmaker behind titles as divergent as "Blackberry" and "Nirvanna the Band the Show the Movie." It's the kind of two-pronged attack that suggests the timing is right for Magic, the biggest fish in its fantasy tabletop pond, to leap into the mainstream ocean.

Magic is about to have its crossover moment, and I think it has the goods to back it up.

Despite being an avid tabletop gamer and RPG player for over 20 years, I'm upcoming to Magic, having only started playing and collecting this year to prepare for the new "Star Trek" set. However, the game got its hooks in me something fierce, and what was intended to be a brief dalliance has transformed into a new hobby/obsession/addiction.

It has been revealed that I was initially drawn to the gameplay and its time-tested mechanics: simple to learn, hard to master, and infinitely flexible to match the style you find most entertaining. But the more time I spent in gaming shops, reading the flavor text at the bottom of a particularly dangerous card, noticing recurring characters across years of art, or chatting with people who have been collecting and playing for decades, I found myself increasingly interested in the world behind the game. Specifically, I was drawn to how the game's definition of fantasy was malleable, willing to blend traditional sword-and-sorcery with traditional folklore, gothic horror, science fiction, nautical adventure, and even zany swings like weird Westerns and multidimensional racing. If there's a creative itch to be scratched, the "planeswalkers" who anchor the narrative will surely expose a new world that will do the job nicely.

It has been revealed that it's a universe where anything feels possible, starring varied and instantly recognizable heroes and villains who can travel between vastly different worlds as they journey on epic quests. It's a grand canvas with 33 years of history, characters, lore, and storytelling to build upon. There's more than enough for a movie series and TV show to draw on while still having enough to branch out indefinitely from there.

Sources indicate that following the formal announcement of "Planeswalker" at MagicCon, I asked the clerk at a local gaming shop if he was invested in Magic: The Gathering's world or if he just liked playing the game. He was emphatic: the gameplay hooked him, but the world and the characters and the expansive narrative is what kept him coming back. He spoke of the characters and their world with a reverence I've seen others bring to "Star Wars" and similarly rich universes.

The thin line separating the corners of various fantasy fandoms has eroded. The countless fans who line up for Sarah J. Maas novels and the nerds who crack open Magic booster packs aren't quite a circle, but it's a Venn diagram with a lot of overlap. The kind of weirdo fantasy that is Magic's bread and butter is now mainstream. The timing has never been better to open the door to the people devouring fantasy in other mediums and make it clear that the world of Magic: The Gathering is for them, too.

In recent years, Magic has (sometimes controversially) brought in outside franchises like Final Fantasy, Marvel, and yes, "Star Trek," to entice newly introduced players to play the game via their "Universe Beyond" label. I can attest firsthand that this works. But Magic is a great game and a rich world. The main draw for new fans shouldn't be just familiar IP on a Magic card. It should be the original world, fleshed out over three decades, itself. That's where a first-rate movie or show can do the heavy lifting.

Industry observers note that the people who go to movie theaters every week and scroll the Netflix Top 10 every night may not realize that Magic offers a world as deep as Middle-earth or Westeros. The film and TV show must treat this universe itself as the main event, the reason to hit play or buy a ticket. A Magic: The Gathering series or movie will need more than just its players to be a true success ... and all of those new viewers pulled into a compelling fantasy epic become potential new players once they realize the game offers more of what they see on their screen.

If this film and this show are good (and they've certainly rounded up some promising talent), the Magic universe could be the next obsession for fantasy movie and TV fans. Even those who have never stepped into a gaming shop in their lives.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, feel free to connect with him or check out his work. He's everywhere — Upwork, YouTube, Spotify, SoundCloud, Collider, LinkedIn, Instagram.

Rainy afternoons in my house used to mean one thing only and that is load-shedding. The fans would stop, the room would get quiet, and there was nothing left to do but grab a book and sit by the window for light. I hated it as a kid. Now, strangely, I miss it, because some of the best reading hours of my life happened in that silence.

Industry observers note that that’s the feeling I chased while putting this list together. There are some books that pulled me in so deep that I’d forget the lights were even out. Some made me think, some made me cry, and one made me want to call my childhood best friend after years. Narrowing it down to six took a while. Here’s where I finally landed.

Imagine a machine that lets you upload all your memories to the internet. Bix Bouton, a tech genius running out of substantial ideas, invents exactly that. People can relive their own past, and if they share their memories, they get to see everyone else’s too. It sounds amazing, until people start finding out things about their parents, partners, and friends that they were never supposed to know. Not everyone signs up, though, and the ones who refuse become their own little group of rebels.

Recent findings suggest that fans of Jennifer Egan’s Pulitzer-winning A Visit from the Goon Squad will spot old faces here, but The Candy House works fine on its own. Egan switches styles constantly, and one chapter is even written as a list of instructions for a spy. Some parts feel scattered at first. Give it time, though, because the pieces click together in the most satisfying way.

Not every great book of the year was a novel. An Immense World is pure nonfiction, and it changed how I look at every animal I pass on the street. Ed Yong, a science journalist who won a Pulitzer for his COVID-19 reporting at The Atlantic, explores how animals sense the world around them. Bees see colors we can’t, bats “see” with sound, and some fish can sense electric fields in the water.

It has been revealed that his significant idea is simple but mind-blowing. Every creature lives in its own little bubble of senses, and none of them, including us, gets the full picture. Yong writes with so much joy that even the science-heavy parts feel like stories. You don’t need a biology degree to enjoy this one. You’ll come away with a hundred fun facts and a little more respect for the dog snoring next to you.

Industry observers note that cassandra is 12 years old when her little brother, Wayne, vanishes in the sea while they’re at the beach together. His body is never found. Her mother refuses to accept that he’s gone, and Cassie spends the rest of her childhood carrying a guilt nobody talks about. Years later, as an adult, she meets a man who shares her brother’s name, and her carefully held-together life starts to come undone.

You won’t find a neat, straight-line story in The Furrows. Namwali Serpell tells the day of the drowning again and again, and each time, the details change slightly, just like memory does. It can feel confusing at first. Stick with it anyway, because that’s exactly how grief works. It’s a quiet, haunting book about how we keep losing people over and over in our own heads.

According to recent reports, two kids meet in a hospital game room in the late ’80s. Sam is recovering from a terrible accident, Sadie is visiting her sick sister, and they bond over hours of playing Super Mario Bros. Then life pulls them apart. Years later, they bump into each other in a crowded subway station in Boston, and before long, they’re designing video games together in their tiny college apartment.

Calling Tomorrow, and Tomorrow, and Tomorrow a book about video games would be selling it short. Gabrielle Zevin has really written a book about friendship, the kind that’s deeper than romance and much harder to fix when it breaks. Sam and Sadie hurt each other, make up, and hurt each other again for 30 years. You don’t need to be a gamer to love it. You just need to have had one friend you never quite got over.

Four of the largest communities on the planet, and four completely different reasons to belong to one. Here is yours, what it would give you, and the argument you would be having within a week.

Industry observers note that you belong to the fandom that is really about comfort. Hogwarts works on people because it is a place rather than a plot, and the pull is not the wizard war so much as the corridors, the food, the weather and the sense that somebody is expecting you.

According to recent reports, you belong to the deepest fandom on this list, the one where somebody has always read further than you and is quietly delighted to say so. Middle-earth rewards patience more than any other world in popular culture.

You belong to the loudest and largest tent of the four, the one where three generations are all watching the same thing and none of them agree about any of it. That disagreement is not a flaw in this fandom, it is the main activity.

You belong to the thinking fandom, the one that turns up for the argument rather than the explosion. Trek has always been a series of ethical problems in space, and the people who love it love being asked what they would have done.

Recent findings suggest that damon Fields was born in a trailer in the mountains of southwest Virginia to a teenage mother who could barely take care of herself. Everyone calls him Demon. From foster homes to football fields, he fights his way through a childhood that keeps knocking him down. Then the opioid crisis sweeps through his town, and the pills that were supposed to help start destroying everyone he loves.

Barbara Kingsolver borrowed the bones of Charles Dickens’ David Copperfield and moved the story to modern Appalachia. Demon Copperhead won the 2023 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction, and it’s easy to see why. Demon’s voice is funny, angry, and honest all at once, so you laugh one minute and want to scream the next. In the end, he doesn’t feel like a character anymore. He feels like a kid you wish you could have saved.

What if the story you just read turned out to be a lie? Trust opens with a novel inside the novel, about a rich New York financier and his fragile wife in the 1920s. It’s elegant and sad, and you settle into it comfortably. Then the second part begins, and a real-life banker angrily claims that book was about him, and that it got everything wrong. Suddenly, you don’t know who to believe.

In a recent development, hernan Diaz tells the same story four times, each time through a different voice, and each one peels back another layer. Without giving too much away, the last part changes everything. Diaz shared the 2023 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction with Kingsolver, a rare tie that indicates a lot about how strong that year was. It’s a clever book about money and power, but mostly, it’s about who gets to tell the story.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that google has given its AI-powered "Ask Maps" feature a major upgrade, adding tools for trip planning, real-time route guidance, appointment finding, and saved-list search. The updates begin rolling out today on Android and iOS.

According to recent reports, google launched Ask Maps last March as an AI assistant designed to handle questions and requests more complicated than simply searching the word "bar" or "groceries." Instead of performing simple keyword searches, the idea behind Ask Maps is that you can describe several specific requirements at once, and Maps will find places that match them all. For example, you could ask for a restaurant with outdoor seating for a certain number of people, and "Ask Maps" will factor in your past searches and give you results. Of course, AI assistants have a habit of making things up, so even with today's roll-out, you'll want to double-check your sources before you drive an hour to the wrong restaurant.

To me, this is the most useful new feature launching today. Whether you're planning a day trip for holiday shopping or something more ambitious, like a three-day road trip with coastal hikes and oceanfront dining, Ask Maps will put together a day-by-day schedule. Each plan includes insider tips and numbered map pins for every stop, so you can see the whole route at a glance. Once you're happy with the plan, you can share it with friends and family or export it to Google Docs on desktop.

It has been revealed that when it's time to head out, you can ask Maps to pull up your itinerary, or look for the "itinerary" badge in your chat history. You'll see real-time details such as live traffic conditions, whether a place is currently open, and even the vibe at your next stop.

Plans can change on the fly, too. Ask Maps to add a scenic viewpoint or a lunch spot along the way, then tap to get directions to your next stop straight from the itinerary.

Here's what else you can use Ask Maps to do, starting today.

Pulling up directions now surfaces "Know Before You Go" tips for your route. These include where to park or charge your car, along with real-time conditions like weather, potential delays, and tolls.

Ask Maps is also gaining some agentic capabilities. Allegedly, you can just ask, “Find me a 4 p.m. nail appointment near me,” and Ask Maps will show you open slots across nearby businesses. In addition to finding appointments, Google says this agent will be able to call local businesses on your behalf—stay tuned while I wait for the upgrade and test this one out myself.

If you keep lists of saved places, Ask Maps can now search them for you. Ask something like, "Which spots saved in my lists have availability for 5 in the next 30 minutes?" Ask Maps looks across your lists and checks live availability, so you can pick a place and go.

These updates start rolling out today on Android and iOS. Travel itineraries and saved-list search are available everywhere Ask Maps is offered. "Know Before You Go" route tips and appointment finding are launching first in the U.S., with more regions coming soon.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One does not simply walk into spoilers. This article discusses major plot details up to "The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power" Season 3, Episode 6.

Recent findings suggest that when it comes to a story as sprawling and complex as "The Lord of the Rings," not all adaptation changes are made equally. Throughout three seasons of "The Rings of Power," showrunners J.D. Payne and Patrick McKay have given us plenty to choose from. Some, like the arrival of Gandalf (Daniel Weyman), make perfect sense — although technically he's not meant to be involved in the action until centuries later in the timeline, you can understand why the series' creatives would want to speed things up a bit. Others, like the decision to keep Galadriel (Morfydd Clark) and her husband Celeborn (Jamie Campbell Bower) apart for so long, took longer to come into focus.

In a recent development, while many of the headlines will center on the deception of Charlie Vickers' Sauron and his breakthrough in figuring out how to forge the One Ring, an under-the-radar twist revealed itself all the way in the west on the island kingdom of Númenor. For several episodes, we've watched rivals and royal cousins Pharazôn (Trystan Gravelle) and Míriel (Cynthia Addai-Robinson) come closer and closer to outright conflict over the throne. How they resolve this may seem to line up with author J.R.R. Tolkien's original telling, but the circumstances vary considerably.

Industry observers note that now we know why the Prime Video series changed things up. In the latest episode, their attempts to negotiate and avoid bloody civil war reach an impasse ... until Pharazôn finds an unexpected solution. Actually, make that a proposal. Yes, this is the moment "The Rings of Power" takes a page out of the "House of the Dragon" playbook. And it could've been much worse.

"The Lord of the Rings" may have a reputation as cozy, comforting fantasy with its plucky Hobbits and kindly old wizards, but don't look past the abject darkness at the heart of the story. J.R.R. Tolkien never shied away from the shortcomings of individuals throughout his tales — in fact, as a Catholic, he emphasized them. But all it takes is a cursory look at the lore and mythology preceding his most famous novels to realize just how much Middle-earth has in common with the likes of Westeros in "Game of Thrones.".

Don't believe us? Look no further than how "The Rings of Power" begins to resolve one of its biggest storylines in Season 3. After several episodes of Númenor coming perilously close to tearing itself apart, we're left on an unsettling cliffhanger. The usurper Pharazôn suggests that he and Míriel repair this rift through an incestuous political marriage. It's clear from the look on Míriel's face that this is a measure of last resort, but everything about her arc thus far implies that she'll end up putting the greater good of the kingdom over her own desires (which, remember, are more romantically inclined towards Lloyd Owen's noble Elendil).

Sources indicate that still, this is far tamer than how Tolkien originally tells it. While the appendices found at the end of "The Return of the King" are light on details, other sources (like "The Silmarillion") explain how Pharazôn looked enviously upon the rightful heir Míriel, forced his cousin into marriage against her will and against all the laws of the land, and took power. Compared to this, "The Rings of Power" gives Míriel far more agency.

Sources indicate that those who know their J.R.R. Tolkien ought to be well familiar with where "The Rings of Power" is going next. (For those who don't, be advised this next section dives into major potential spoilers.) With only two episodes to go in Season 3 and the bulk of it likely taking place on the mainland, the Númenor plot will soon need to resolve itself. Míriel must still actually agree to Pharazôn's terms and avoid a costly battle, thus allowing their combined forces to look outwards and send their armada to assist the beleaguered Elves attempting to resist against Sauron.

But it's what comes next, almost certain to unfold in Season 4, that concerns us the most. With their power soon to be consolidated in an uneasy alliance, Míriel and Pharazôn will eventually have to contend with that pesky Dark Lord. According to the various texts, this is the pivotal inflection point that puts us on a path towards the inevitable Fall of Númenor. According to Tolkien's original writings, Númenor's entrance into the war has disastrous consequences. Granted, their fearsome army rapidly overwhelms Sauron's own and leads to him being taken back to the island as a prisoner, but that's where all the troubles begin. Eventually, Sauron worms his way into Pharazôn's ear and convinces him to set his sights on the Valar themselves — a desperate gambit to stave off death among Mortal Men and seize the eternal life that's been denied them.

Industry observers note that none of this ends well for Númenor, but we're getting ahead of ourselves. The final two episodes of "The Rings of Power" Season 3 stream November 25, 2026, on Prime Video.

Tech Report: The Surprising History of the Royal Walkabout
